timeline.event: Saturation bell team of three locks out from DSV Bibby Topaz at the Huntington field (central North Sea, block 22/14b). Chris Lemons (then 32) and Dave/David Yuasa are working inside a subsea drilling template / manifold ('Huntington manifold'), removing and replacing pipework and doing valve and pressure testing. Duncan Allcock is bellman in the bell, and dive supervisor Craig Frederick is in dive control on the ship. The 2022 case report says the bell undocked at 20:13. Lemons says it was about 10pm and they had been diving 'for about an hour'. Frederick says the alarm came about 45 minutes into the work.

A series of DP alarms sounds, linked to the Kongsberg K-Pos RBUS communication bus. The bridge declares amber, which is soon upgraded to red. The dive supervisor orders both divers out of the structure and back to the bell staging. The vessel loses position and drifts (east, per IMCA).

Both divers climb on top of the template. Lemons' umbilical snags under a transponder bucket / metal outcrop on the (west) side of the structure, and he asks for slack. Yuasa is dragged away by his own umbilical and gets within about a metre of Lemons. In the bell, Allcock cannot pull in slack because the umbilical is so taut it is pulling a steel rack off the bell wall. Lemons' account of the order: the gas hose kinks, so he opens his bailout; then the comms line goes; then the umbilical parts 'like a shotgun' and his light goes out. Comms and video to Lemons were lost at about 22:12 (Bibby statement), or the umbilical severed at 22:13 (case report).

Lemons falls onto the seabed on his back in total darkness, too dark to read his gauge. He finds the structure by bumping into it and pulls himself up an old hose to the top. The bell is gone. He estimates he has used 2-3 minutes of bailout, curls up / lies in a fetal position, and later loses consciousness. The time he blacked out is unknown. Allcock pulls in the severed end of the umbilical, and STV reports him shouting 'I've lost my diver'. Yuasa makes his way back to the bell and waits under it.

The Master and Chief Officer take manual control of the thrusters after the vessel has drifted about 240 m, and head back toward the template. Engineers confirm the fault is in the DP control system, not the thrusters. Later, DP power is recycled (Lemons calls it a 'hard reset') and full auto DP returns. Reported drift distances differ: 240 m (Bibby 2012 and IMCA), 190 m (Bibby 2015), about 200 m (STV), 250 m (Frederick).

The diver locator beacon and the ROV place Lemons on top of the template. Crew on the ship watch him on the ROV feed, Lemons says over 100 people. He is seen moving and twitching, then still. The case report reconstructs that he was waving with bubbles visible at about 22 minutes and was motionless about 3 minutes later. Lemons says the ROV reached him 'not long after I fell unconscious'. Yuasa proposed a rescue from about 50 m away, and Frederick refused because of the risk to a second diver.

The vessel is back close to the drilling template and the bell is lowered as close as possible. Yuasa leaves the bell stage, under ROV watch. The case report puts the template only about 18 m from the bell.

Yuasa checks Lemons is not still attached and hauls him to the bell. The Independent quotes Yuasa putting a hose from his own supply into Lemons' helmet. Both divers are on the bell stage at 22:46 and Lemons is inside the bell at 22:48 (Bibby). The case report gives helmet removal at 22:46, 33 minutes after the umbilical parted. Allcock removes the helmet ('blue as a pair of denim jeans', in Allcock's words), blocks the nose and gives two mouth-to-mouth breaths, and Lemons gasps and comes round. Bibby's 2012 statement and IMCA instead say he was 'unconscious but breathing' and regained consciousness once the helmet came off.

He is warmed with hot water in the bell, and the ROV surveys the bell umbilical and wires before the bell is recovered. The case report has the transfer to the chamber at about 23:38. In the chamber he gets therapeutic oxygen, blankets and a heating mat, and an IV attempt fails, per Lemons' slides. A medic and the shore diving doctor are consulted, and the case report says he was stable by about 02:00. The case report says decompression began at 07:45 on 19 September and the Topaz sailed back to Aberdeen (about 15 hours).

Decompression completes on 22 September (the case report says after 78 h; Lemons says '4 days'). Lemons has hospital checks on 23 September, and all divers get a clean bill of health, with no neurological injury found.

Bibby Offshore's incident timeline is circulated (reposted on gCaptain) and UK press report the story (Telegraph/Mail, via OilPrice and AOL): '262 ft (80 m)', '38 minutes' / 'almost 40 minutes', '115 miles off Aberdeenshire'. Bibby said it had notified the authorities and was running its own investigation (Energy Voice 2012, seen only as a search snippet).
Lemons, Yuasa and Allcock go back to the same site and finish the job. The exact date is not published.

A Bibby Topaz incident summary slide deck dated 08.10.12 is posted on SlideShare (Villazon Granda). The case report calls it the 'official investigation' reconstruction. CADC summarised it: depth 91 m, snag on the transponder bucket, diver 'unconscious and breathing'.

IMCA Safety Flash 02/13, 'Serious DP Diving Incident', is anonymised but matches every detail: 90 m, drilling template, transponder bucket, 240 m drift, K-Pos RBUS. It says the investigation was a joint effort by the contractor, the DP manufacturer, the class society and the regulator. It found the RBUS jammed through faults in I/O modules in the DPC-3 cabinet, with no definitive root cause, plus hardware faults: a loose fuse, grounding currents, a shield not earthed, and the cabinet not earthed to the hull. The fix was a firmware update kit. The UK HSE Offshore Safety Division issued Safety Notice OSD 1-2013, warning that a single fault can block dual-bus DP communications on an IMO class 2 DSV.

Lemons marries his fiancee Morag Martin. The BBC and People say a few months after the accident. Reader's Digest (seen only as a search snippet) says the wedding was set for the following April. The case report instead says the return to diving came 'just after his marriage', which conflicts.

Bibby Offshore commissions 'Lifeline', a roughly 45-minute industry safety film by Floating Harbour, mixing real-time footage and reconstruction. Bibby also sets up a Diving Safety Workgroup, decided by Sir Michael Bibby and CEO Howard Woodcock.

JFD COBRA bailout rebreathers are deployed operationally from Bibby Topaz. Lemons said in 2019 'we also introduced the COBRA', which gives far more emergency gas than open-circuit bailout. These details come from search snippets of trade press.

The documentary 'Last Breath' (directors Richard da Costa and Alex Parkinson; distributed by Dogwoof; music by Paul Leonard-Morgan) opens in UK cinemas and on Netflix. BBC Scotland broadcast it on 7 May 2019. It uses real helmet-camera, ROV and comms footage and audio.

Dreyer, Deussen, Berndt and Schipke publish 'How to Survive 33 min after the Umbilical of a Saturation Diver Severed at a Depth of 90 msw?' in Healthcare 10(3):453. It is a reconstruction based on calculations and on phone interviews with Lemons.

The dramatised feature 'Last Breath' is released (directed by Alex Parkinson; Focus Features / Entertainment Film Distributors). Finn Cole plays Lemons, Woody Harrelson plays Allcock, Simu Liu plays Yuasa, and Mark Bonnar plays 'Craig'.
CBC Radio The Current (host Matt Galloway) airs an interview with Lemons (about 19:46) plus a written piece. Physiologist Jochen Schipke is also quoted. The segment headline says '25 minutes'.

key_facts.fact: DATE / TIME: Tuesday 18 September 2012, at night. Company timeline: alarms ~22:10, umbilical parted ~22:12-22:13, back near the template 22:40, Lemons in the bell 22:46-22:48 (ship time, presumably BST). Lemons told OGV 'it was 10pm'. OUTLIER: one BBC News 2019 quote has Lemons saying 'at two in the morning', which contradicts every company and technical source. Do not use it.

LOCATION: Huntington oil field, UKCS block 22/14b, central North Sea. Field operator: E.ON E&P UK (first oil April 2013, so the field was still being commissioned in 2012). Distances given: about 204-205 km / 127 miles east of Aberdeen (BBC Future, i, offshore-technology); 200 km (case report); '115 miles off the east coast of Aberdeenshire' (2012 press); 'east of Peterhead' (BBC); '90 miles east of Aberdeen' (Lemons' own 2025 slides). Safest wording: 'about 200 km east of Aberdeen'. Bibby's client relationship with E.ON is not confirmed.

DEPTH (all reported values): 80 m / 262 ft (2012 press); 90 m (Bibby 2015, IMCA SF 02/13, 2022 case report); 91 m (BBC News 'lowered 91m', CADC; Lemons' slides say '91 metres (275 feet)', a unit error since 91 m is about 299 ft); 'almost 100 m / about 300 ft' (BBC News); 100 m / 328 ft (BBC Future, CBC); 330 ft (Undercurrent, Entertainment Weekly). Field water depth is about 91 m, and Yuasa says the team was stored at 100 m. Recommended: '수심 약 90m' (about 90 m), noting that some reports say 100 m.

VESSEL: DSV Bibby Topaz (Bibby Offshore, later renamed Rever Offshore). About 107 m long and about 8,000 t (Lemons himself says '8,000 tonne vessel'), with a hull saturation system (Dräger) and a crew of about 130 (case report). DP system: Kongsberg K-Pos, IMO equipment class 2 (HSE/IMCA). A gCaptain forum poster's 'DP3' claim is unverified.

DP FAILURE CAUSE: The communication bus (RBUS) between the DP control computers and the I/O modules jammed. I/O went to failsafe, which commanded zero thrust, and gyro and position inputs dropped out. The investigation found faults in one or more RBUS I/O modules in the DPC-3 cabinet but 'no definitive cause'. Hardware faults included a loose fuse connection, grounding current, an unearthed shield, and the cabinet not bonded to the hull. Fix: a Kongsberg RBUS I/O firmware update. HSE said the probable cause was a single fault blocking internal data communications. The weather drove the drift but did not cause the failure, and the ship was not storm-damaged.

WEATHER: Bibby's 2012 statement gives 30 knots from 316 degrees, sea state 5. Case report: Beaufort 7, 4 m waves. BBC News and the i: 35-knot winds, with a 5 m swell (i). Lemons' slides: 35 knots, 6 m swell. Frederick called it 'pretty standard' for September and 'not even at the outside limit' for diving. Lemons: 'The sea was a little rough on the surface, but it was pretty clear underwater.' Sea temperature: 3 C (BBC News), 'probably below 3C' (BBC Future), 4 C (Lemons' slides), 4-5 C (case report).

BELL TEAM AND KEY PEOPLE: Chris Lemons, 32 (the i says 33; use 32), 'Diver 2'. Born in Edinburgh and grew up in Cambridge per the i; BBC says 'Edinburgh-born'; CBC quotes 'I grew up ... in Cambridge'. He had about 8-10 years as a commercial diver but only about 18 months / 9 deep dives in saturation (BBC Future, i, OGV); the case report and CBC say 10 years' experience. Dave/David Yuasa ('Diver 1'), described as very experienced; formerly a scuba instructor in Asia and Cornwall. Duncan Allcock ('Diver 3', bellman), Lemons' mentor, trained at Fort William in 1985. Dive supervisor: Craig Frederick (Canadian), named in the BBC quote ('dive supervisor Craig') and in the documentary credits. Bridge: the Master and Chief Officer drove the ship manually. Documentary listings name Michal Cichorski as DP officer and Kevin Whyte as ROV pilot (from film databases only). Bibby lead QHSE adviser Chris Cleghorn was on board. Spelling: the BBC's 'Youasa' is wrong; it is Yuasa.

UMBILICAL CONTENTS: breathing gas (heliox), hot water for the hot-water suit, comms, light/power and video, with a strength rope through the middle (BBC Future). Diameter about 4.5 cm (case report). LENGTH is disputed: 27 m (case report), 45 m (CBC), 50 m (Yuasa and Frederick, quoted in the Independent and The National). Yuasa's rule of thumb is about 1 minute of bailout per 10 m of umbilical.

SNAG POINT: a transponder bucket with a metal outcrop on the (west) face of the drilling template. Lemons says it 'should have been removed' and 'shouldn't have been there'. Also confirmed by IMCA and CADC. Lemons' umbilical was stretched until it parted, and Allcock says it was bending or pulling the 'four-inch stainless-steel' rack off the bell wall.

BAILOUT DURATION (all values): Lemons himself has given 'five, maybe six minutes' (BBC News 2019; OGV 2019, '5-6 minutes'), 'six or seven minutes' (BBC Future 2019) and 'eight or nine minutes' (CBC 2025). Frederick, by his own reckoning, says 10 minutes and that legally only five were needed (Independent). Director Parkinson: at least 5, maybe 7-8, 'no way more than 10' (EW 2025). Most media say 'five minutes'. The case report says the set was two 12 L, 300 bar cylinders of heliox 86/14 (about 7,000 L usable). It argues that '5 minutes' is physiologically impossible and calculates about 13 minutes at hard-work breathing, longer as he calmed and then breathed shallowly while unconscious. Their conclusion is that there may have been no real 'gas gap'; this is a model, not a measurement. Hardware: open-circuit cylinders on his back, opened by a knob on the helmet. It was NOT a rebreather.

WHAT HE DID: He fell back onto the seabed in total darkness, too dark to read his gauge. He groped around, bumped into the structure, and climbed back on top using an old hose. Height of the climb: case report says a 5 m platform; Frederick says the template was about 11 m high. He looked up for the bell and saw no light. He chose to stay calm and conserve gas, and curled up / lay in a fetal position on top so he could be found. He then felt breathing get harder and lost consciousness. Lemons' own words include 'A quiet resignation came over me' (BBC News 2019) and 'I felt it coming ... and then: nothing' (quoted in the case report).

TIME FROM UMBILICAL PARTING TO RESCUE (all values): about 33 min (case report, 22:13 to 22:46); about 34-36 min (Bibby timeline, ~22:12 to 22:46-22:48); 35 min (BBC News 2019; Lemons' website); '36 or 37 minutes' to resuscitation (Parkinson, EW 2025); 38 min (2012 Telegraph/Mail via OilPrice; Undercurrent; Business Insider); 'almost 40' / 40 (2012 press; Bibby 2015); 'over 40' (Divernet 2026); Lemons' 2025 slides mark 35 and 41 minutes. TIME WITHOUT BREATHABLE GAS OR UNCONSCIOUS is a separate and unknown figure: 'about half an hour' (CBC, BBC Future, i, STV), '25 minutes' (CBC audio title; People 'over 25'), '29 minutes' (2025 film). Parkinson: 'the actual exact figure of when he passed out, no one actually knows.' Recommended wording: 'about 35 minutes after his lifeline snapped; most of it with his emergency gas gone (exact time unknown)'.

RESCUE SEQUENCE: (1) The bridge regains manual thruster control about 5 minutes in (22:17), about 240 m off station. (2) The locator beacon and the ROV find Lemons on top of the template, and the crew watch the live feed. (3) DP power is recycled ('hard reset') and auto DP restored, and the ship is back over the site at about 22:40, roughly 28 minutes after the parting. (4) The bell is lowered close; Yuasa goes out, checks Lemons is free (and, per the Independent, feeds him gas through a hose into his helmet), and hauls him to the bell, where Lemons says Yuasa 'popped my head back in to the diving bell'. (5) Allcock pulls the helmet off; Lemons is blue; Allcock gives two mouth-to-mouth breaths; Lemons gasps and comes round. DISPUTE: the 2022 case report's narrative says 'D2' (Yuasa) gave the two breaths, but its own Discussion credits the bellman. Every first-hand account (Lemons, Allcock, the BBC) says Allcock gave them. Company and IMCA reports say 'unconscious but breathing', while BBC Future says 'not breathing'; the case report says 'slow and shallow breathing'.

MEDICAL EXPLANATIONS (all are HYPOTHESES; none is proven): (a) Cold. The 3-5 C water, the loss of suit hot water, and heliox's high heat capacity cooled him and lowered his oxygen demand. Mike Tipton (Portsmouth) told BBC Future that cooling the brain to 30 C can extend survival from 10 to 20 minutes. Schipke's case report calculated a core temperature of 28.8-27.2 C; this was COMPUTED, not measured, although CBC states it as fact. (b) High-oxygen heliox 'saturating tissues'. This is Lemons' and Frederick's own belief; the case report calculates that dissolved oxygen in blood adds only about 1 minute, but estimates about 18 L of total body, lung and helmet oxygen. (c) A bigger bailout than '5 minutes', plus calm and then very shallow breathing (case report, Schipke). (d) Possible helium neuroprotection (case report; based only on animal and in-vitro studies). (e) Selective brain cooling (the i, 'experts' unnamed). (f) Altered oxygen-transport gene activity in saturation divers (Ingrid Eftedal, NTNU, BBC Future; speculative). (g) 'Hypercapnic protection', a question Lemons lists in his talks. (h) Director Parkinson's 'stasis at the precise temperature' (People), which is a layman's claim. Lemons: 'there is no concrete explanation'; Frederick: 'how he survived, I'll never know for sure.'

INVESTIGATIONS: Bibby notified the authorities and ran its own investigation; Lemons: 'there was an investigation in to the cause'. IMCA Safety Flash 02/13 (January 2013, anonymised) describes a joint investigation by the contractor, the DP manufacturer, the classification society and the regulator. UK HSE Offshore Safety Division Safety Notice OSD 1-2013 (23 Jan 2013) is also anonymised. A 2015 HSE presentation lists the same case, but labels it 'DSV drift-off, West of Shetland, October 2010', which looks like a labelling error; its 90 m, drilling-template and severed-umbilical details match. No HSE prosecution or published full report was found. The case report cites a SlideShare 'Incident Summary 08.10.12 Bibby Topaz' as the official reconstruction. The anonymised IMCA and HSE documents are linked to the Topaz by matching details, not by name.

SAFETY CHANGES: IMCA lists the contractor's follow-up review items: bell staging and equipment for recovering an unconscious diver, diver locator beacons, thermal undersuits, the bailout bottle specification, diver rebreathers, extra life support on the seabed, the ROV interface for rescue, DP software and hardware verification, manual driving trials, and drills. Bibby formed a Diving Safety Workgroup and made the film 'Lifeline'. Lemons says the team 'introduced the COBRA' bailout rebreather: 'instead of 5 minutes you would now have 40 minutes'. Trade press of April 2018 reports COBRA used from the Topaz. BBC Future's claim that divers industry-wide 'now' carry 40-minute bailout, and that umbilicals have 'fairy lights', is not independently verified.

VERIFIED ON-RECORD QUOTES (for subtitles and voice-clip matching). These quotes come from the published text. Check the actual audio before using any of them as a clip. LEMONS to CBC The Current, 22 Mar 2025: 'All of a sudden ... I'd become an anchor, basically, to an 8,000 tonne vessel. And obviously there's only going to be one winner in that situation.' / 'That had a strangely calming effect, I think, knowing that I couldn't do much to help myself.' / 'I resigned myself quite quickly to the fact that this was probably going to be ... the place that I die.' / 'It was very much a normal day at the office.' / 'I stay in the dry and the safe.' LEMONS to BBC Scotland, 2019: 'I realised very quickly that the end was nigh. I was on a countdown clock and it was counting very fast.' / 'A quiet resignation came over me.' LEMONS to BBC Future, 2019: 'One of the greatest reasons I survived was the quality of the people around me.' ALLCOCK (Independent, 2019): 'He's a bald guy, he's half frozen to death, and he's gone as blue as a pair of denim jeans.' YUASA (Independent): 'It's safe as long as everything goes right. And if it goes wrong, it's instantly dangerous.' FREDERICK (Independent): 'I have total confidence this isn't a recovery mission, it's a rescue mission.'

WHAT LEMONS SAID HE THOUGHT (his own published words only, which the narration may paraphrase with attribution): sadness and disbelief; thinking of the people at home and 'the chaos I would cause' (BBC News); 'apologising a lot to my fiancée Morag' (BBC Future); 'how've I ended up dying in this dark, lonely place?' (CBC); 'I hoped death wouldn't hurt' (paraphrased in the i and STV). The 'This is my last breath' line comes SECOND-HAND from director Parkinson (EW), so attribute it to Parkinson or avoid it. On waking, per Parkinson, Lemons said 'Are you okay, Dave? What's happened?' This is also second-hand.

facts.aftermath:
Medically: once his helmet was off and he had two rescue breaths from Allcock, Lemons came round within moments, groggy ('a groggy, drunken feeling', the i). He was warmed with hot water in the bell, then transferred to the saturation chamber, where he was given therapeutic oxygen. His own slides list an attempted (failed) IV line, some vomiting, bruising and sleepiness. BBC Future reports only 'a couple of bruises on his legs'. He decompressed for about 3-4 days with the team (finished 22 Sept 2012), had hospital checks on 23 Sept, and was given a clean bill of health with no detectable neurological injury; the case report adds that he later passed cognitive testing.

Back to work: about three weeks later, he, Yuasa and Allcock went back to the same site to finish the job. Lemons, BBC, BBC Future, CBC and director Parkinson all say so; Parkinson calls it '100 percent true'. Lemons told OGV the team had decided together to return: 'if we didn't do it then, perhaps we never would.'

Personal life: he married his then-fiancée Morag Martin 'a few months later' (BBC 2019, People 2025); Reader's Digest said the wedding was set for April 2013. The 2022 case report's line about the return coming 'just after his marriage' conflicts with this. They have a daughter (BBC Future 2019; do not name or depict her). In 2019 he lived near Mallaig on Scotland's west coast. He kept saturation diving for about 10 more years (CBC; People says until 2022) and then became a dive supervisor. Parkinson (2025) says he 'works occasionally on the ship the accident happened on'. In his own words: 'I stay in the dry and the safe' (CBC 2025). He gives keynote talks (chrislemons.co.uk; NIBA 2025; GO Diving Show main stage, Feb/Mar 2026). He told CBC there were 'no great epiphanies', only 'a more acute awareness' of death, and told BBC Future, 'I don't see it as something to be feared any more.'

Industry: Bibby Offshore (later Rever Offshore) set up a Diving Safety Workgroup and commissioned the roughly 45-minute industry film 'Lifeline' (Floating Harbour, 2013, publicised in 2015). IMCA Safety Flash 02/13 and HSE Safety Notice OSD 1-2013 (both anonymised) spread the DP data-bus lesson, and Kongsberg issued a firmware fix. COBRA bailout rebreathers were later used on the Topaz (2018).

Screen: the documentary 'Last Breath' (2019; Richard da Costa and Alex Parkinson; MetFilm / Floating Harbour / Crab Apple / Backflip; Dogwoof in the UK; Netflix; BBC Scotland 7 May 2019). It used real helmet-camera, ROV and comms footage and audio, plus interviews and reconstructions. The feature film 'Last Breath' (2025; Alex Parkinson; Focus Features in the US from 28 Feb 2025; Entertainment Film Distributors in the UK from 14 Mar 2025) stars Finn Cole as Lemons, Woody Harrelson as Allcock and Simu Liu as Yuasa. It dramatises events and invents some characters and details, so treat it as fiction, and do not use footage or music from either film. Everyone involved survived. The 2022 case report (Dreyer et al., Healthcare) argues that the survival is explainable rather than a 'miracle', while stressing that 'the limit for a healthy outcome was very close.'
myths: 'He survived 30-40 minutes with no oxygen.' This merges two figures. About 33-38 minutes passed between the umbilical parting and the rescue, but he was breathing bailout gas for part of that time. How long he actually went without breathable gas, or was unconscious, is unknown (Parkinson: 'no one actually knows').

'He had exactly five minutes of oxygen.' Five minutes is the commonly quoted legal or nominal figure. Lemons has said 5-6, 6-7 and 8-9 minutes at different times, Frederick says 10, and the case report argues the 2 x 12 L, 300 bar set could last far longer than 5 minutes.
'Oxygen tank' / 'breathing oxygen.' He breathed heliox (helium-oxygen) from the umbilical and from open-circuit bailout cylinders. Bailout heliox at that depth was about 14% O2.
'He had a closed-circuit rebreather' (Undercurrent 2019). He did not; he had open-circuit bailout cylinders. Rebreathers (COBRA) were introduced afterwards.
'Saturation divers now carry 40 minutes of bailout industry-wide' (BBC Future caption). This is not verified. It reflects his own company's adoption of the COBRA rebreather, as Lemons describes it.

'The ship was damaged in a heavy storm' (People 2025). The DP control system's data bus jammed. Wind of about 30-35 knots drove the drift, but Frederick called the weather 'pretty standard', within diving limits.
'Dive supervisor Craig Frederick was in the diving bell' (People 2025). Wrong: Duncan Allcock was the bellman, and Frederick was in dive control on the ship.

'The structure he was attached to began to detach from the seabed' (The National, 2019 caption). There is no basis for this; his umbilical snagged on a transponder bucket on a seabed drilling template.
'He was working on an oil rig.' He was on a subsea drilling template / manifold on the seabed, about 90 m down, supported from a dive support vessel, not a platform rig.
'It happened at two in the morning' (a quote in the BBC News 2019 article). The company timeline puts it at about 22:10-22:48 on 18 September, and Lemons elsewhere says '10pm'.

'Yuasa gave the rescue breaths' (the 2022 case report's narrative section). First-hand accounts from Lemons and Allcock, and the BBC, all say Allcock, the bellman, did; the case report's own Discussion also credits the bellman.
'His body temperature was measured at 27 C' (CBC wording). 28.8-27.2 C is a CALCULATED estimate in the case report, not a measurement.

'The 2025 film shows what happened.' It is dramatised. A flare lighting the seabed, Yuasa telling him to switch to a 10-minute backup, Lemons tying himself to the manifold, the ROV trying to lift him, and captain 'Andre Jenson' are cinematic or fictional (Parkinson admits the flare was for cinematic reasons).
'It's a BBC documentary.' 'Last Breath' (2019) was an independent production (MetFilm, Floating Harbour and others), released by Dogwoof and Netflix, and only broadcast on BBC Scotland.
'He was clinically dead / died and came back.' No reliable source documents cardiac arrest. Reports say he was unconscious, blue, and not breathing or breathing slowly and shallowly.
'He went straight home and never saw a doctor' (2025 film). He spent about 4 days in decompression under medical monitoring, then had hospital checks (Bibby statement; Parkinson in EW).
Parkinson's claims that Lemons had earlier near-death experiences (an avalanche, being swept out to sea) are second-hand and uncorroborated. Do not use them.
The quote 'Chris said he knew to try and conserve his gas...' in 2012 press (OilPrice) is attributed only to 'the diver' and its source is unclear. Do not use it.
facts.sensitivities:
Everyone survived; the people named are living private individuals: Lemons, his wife Morag Martin and their daughter, Yuasa, Allcock and Frederick. Do not depict or name the daughter. Do not draw recognisable likenesses; use generic diver silhouettes in helmets. Do not show company logos (Bibby / Rever Offshore, Kongsberg).

The real ROV footage of Lemons convulsing on the template is distressing; the filmmakers themselves called it 'grim' and at risk of being 'voyeuristic'. It is also copyrighted (documentary / Floating Harbour / Bibby). Do not reproduce it, recreate the convulsions in detail, or show his blue face. Suggest the moment instead: stillness, the ROV light, the bubbles stopping. Do not use any audio, footage or music from 'Last Breath' (2019) or 'Last Breath' (2025), including the real comms audio ('I've lost my diver'). Short interview clips of Lemons' own voice are usable with on-screen attribution (outlet and date) and Korean subtitles that match the audio verbatim. The best candidate is CBC Radio The Current, 22 Mar 2025, interview by Matt Galloway (segment about 19:46). Podcast interviews also exist (Real Risk on Buzzsprout, Taproom Talks, Roll With The Punches ep. 242, Newstalk). Check the exact wording against the audio, because published text can differ from what was said.

Inner thoughts: use only what Lemons has said publicly, and attribute it (for example '레몬스는 훗날 BBC에 말했다…', 'Lemons later told the BBC…'). Phrases with good sourcing: resignation, sadness, thinking of the people at home, apologising to Morag. 'This is my last breath' is only reported second-hand by the director. Do not write dialogue for Yuasa, Allcock, the bridge crew or the ROV pilot; quote only their published words, and note that Allcock's quotes include profanity.

Blame: the investigation found DP data-bus jamming plus hardware faults with no definitive root cause. It did not find operator error. Do not blame the DP officers, the master or the supervisor, and credit the bridge, ROV and dive team as every source does.

Numbers: depth (80 / 90 / 91 / 100 m), bailout (5-10 min), rescue time (33-41 min) and distance from Aberdeen all vary. Recommended on-screen wording: '수심 약 90m' (depth about 90 m), '비상 기체 약 5~10분 (출처마다 다름)' (emergency gas about 5-10 minutes; sources vary), '생명줄이 끊긴 뒤 약 35분 만에 구조' (rescued about 35 minutes after his lifeline snapped), '언제 의식을 잃었는지는 아무도 모른다' (no one knows when he lost consciousness). Say 'breathing gas' (호흡 기체, heliox), not 'oxygen'. Present the survival explanations as hypotheses ('가설', 'hypothesis'); do not call it a miracle as fact, and do not say science has 'solved' it either. The case report authors themselves say it was 'very close'.

Korean terminology: 포화잠수 (saturation diving), 다이빙 벨 (diving bell), 엄빌리컬/생명줄 (umbilical / lifeline), 동적위치제어(DP) (dynamic positioning), 비상 기체 실린더/베일아웃 (bailout cylinder), 원격조종 무인잠수정(ROV) (ROV), 벨맨 (bellman), 잠수 감독관 (dive supervisor). Name spellings: 크리스 레몬스 (Chris Lemons), 데이브(데이비드) 유아사 (Dave/David Yuasa), 던컨 올콕 (Duncan Allcock), 크레이그 프레드릭 (Craig Frederick), 비비 토파즈 (Bibby Topaz), 헌팅턴 유전 (Huntington field).

Source access note: the Guardian (Sam Wollaston's 2019 interview and Leslie Felperin's review of 5 Apr 2019), The Times (30 Mar 2019), Energy Voice and Reader's Digest could not be read directly (paywalls or bot blocks), so details attributed to them here come from search snippets or citations elsewhere. Snippets attributed to the Guardian piece: '90 metres (295ft)'; Allcock 'began administering CPR'. All other key facts were read in the primary text: BBC News, BBC Future, CBC, the i, STV, OGV, the Independent via Yahoo, The National, the PMC case report, the IMCA PDF, the HSE notice and Bibby's 2012 statement.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: We had a constant line of communication with dive supervisor Craig - up in the ship - through an earpiece in our helmets. The first and only indication was to hear the alarm sounding in dive control, which was not unusual because they test them. But it was quickly followed by Craig asking us to get out of the structure, get on top of it and get back to the diving bell as quickly as we could and we could tell from the urgency in his voice that this wasn't a drill, this was something serious.
quotes.context: Lemons describing the moment the alarm sounded (Bibby Topaz DP failure, 18 Sep 2012). Interview with BBC Scotland News, article by Debbie Jackson, 5 Apr 2019. LADbible (9 Jan 2025) re-quotes the last sentence as 'told the BBC in April 2019'.
reported_by: BBC News Scotland, 'Diver cheated death in North Sea miracle', 5 Apr 2019 https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-north-east-orkney-shetland-47826802
quotes.korean: 헬멧 속 이어피스로 배 위의 잠수 감독관 크레이그와 늘 교신이 열려 있었어요. 처음이자 유일한 신호는 잠수 통제실에서 울리는 경보음이었는데, 경보는 시험 삼아 울리기도 해서 이상한 일이 아니었죠. 그런데 곧바로 크레이그가 구조물에서 나와서, 그 위로 올라가서, 최대한 빨리 다이빙 벨로 돌아가라고 했어요. 그 목소리의 다급함만으로 알 수 있었어요. 훈련이 아니라는 걸. 정말 심각한 일이라는 걸.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: On that day our supervisor Craig was very quickly insisting we remove ourselves from the structure and you could just tell from the urgency in his voice and the tone of his voice that this wasn't routine, it wasn't a drill.
quotes.context: REAL AUDIO candidate (his own voice, interview, not documentary). BBC Radio 5 Live podcast 'Eye of the Storm' with Emma Barnett, 'Diver who cheated death', released 4 Jun 2019. In downloaded file p07c6w6z (1327 s) approx 04:33-04:46 (medium-model word timing). ASR transcript; confirm by ear.
reported_by: BBC Radio 5 Live, Eye of the Storm, p07c6y6b (podcast version p07c6w6z), my faster-whisper transcript
quotes.korean: 그날 감독관 크레이그가 아주 다급하게 구조물에서 빠져나오라고 했어요. 목소리의 긴박함과 톤만으로 알 수 있었죠. 평소 일이 아니라는 걸. 훈련이 아니라는 걸.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: You could just tell from the tone of his voice that this was something fairly serious, not a drill. I don't remember really calculating what was going on, but you could tell something was afoot.
quotes.context: CBC Radio 'The Current' with Matt Galloway, podcast episode 'Stranded, this diver lost oxygen for 25 minutes. He survived', 17 Mar 2025 (web article by Abby Hughes 22 Mar 2025 prints a shortened form: 'You could just tell from the tone of his voice that this was something fairly … serious'). Words here follow the podscripts.co machine transcript of the audio. CBC audio file not obtained.
quotes.korean: 목소리 톤만 들어도 꽤 심각한 일이라는 걸, 훈련이 아니라는 걸 알 수 있었어요. 무슨 일인지 따져본 기억은 없지만, 뭔가 벌어지고 있다는 건 느껴졌죠.

quotes.speaker: Craig Frederick (dive supervisor)
quotes.words_en: The dynamic positioning officer, the DPO, on that night he just said look we've got an amber light and just by the way he said it, it occurred to me that this was quite serious. [...] My only concern is Diver 1 and Diver 2. So I just told them to drop their tools and get out of the structure, not realising exactly what was going to happen in the next minute or so.
quotes.context: REAL AUDIO candidate, supervisor's own voice (interview). BBC World Service Outlook podcast 'How did this diver cheat death?', presenter Emily Webb, 23 Apr 2019. Downloaded podcast file p0776q29 (2140 s, starts with a ~13 s trailer): approx 10:16-10:25 and 10:45-10:53. CAUTION: between them the presenter introduces 'a recording from the day' (Dogwoof-licensed documentary/comms audio); do not use that part.
reported_by: BBC World Service Outlook, p0776rqm / p08lg86l (podcast) and w3csyhqc (broadcast), my faster-whisper transcript
quotes.korean: 그날 밤 DP 담당 항해사가 '앰버 등이 떴다'고만 했는데, 그 말투만으로 이게 꽤 심각하다는 생각이 들었어요. […] 제 관심사는 오직 1번 다이버와 2번 다이버였어요. 그래서 공구를 버리고 구조물에서 나오라고만 했죠. 그 후 1분 남짓 사이에 무슨 일이 벌어질지는 정확히 모른 채로요.

quotes.speaker: Craig Frederick (dive supervisor)
quotes.words_en: So, I just kept saying, 'You've got to get back to the bell! Get on top of the structure!'
quotes.context: Frederick recalling his instructions as the alarm went from amber to red. Interview by Stephen Applebaum, The Independent, published 15 Apr 2019 (read via Yahoo syndication). These are his recollected words, not a recording.
reported_by: The Independent / Yahoo News, 'Last Breath: Real-life drama of the North Sea diver who cheated death', Stephen Applebaum, 15 Apr 2019 https://news.yahoo.com/last-breath-real-life-drama-130514791.html
quotes.korean: 그래서 계속 외쳤어요. '벨로 돌아가야 해! 구조물 위로 올라가!'

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: You had 8,000 tonnes of boat essentially pulling against you and I was basically an anchor to that in the bottom and there was only going to be one winner in that circumstance.
quotes.context: Umbilical snagged on the manifold while the drifting ship pulled. BBC Scotland News, 5 Apr 2019. Similar wording on CBC 2025 ('I'd become an anchor, basically, to an 8,000 tonne vessel... only going to be one winner') and GB News 15 Mar 2025.
quotes.korean: 8천 톤짜리 배가 저를 잡아당기고 있었고, 저는 사실상 바닥에 박힌 닻이었어요. 그런 상황에서 이길 쪽은 하나뿐이었죠.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: It was trapped and on the other end of that umbilical was 8,000 tons of boat and I was effectively acting as an anchor at that point. And I think that's the point I realized suddenly that this had become very very serious indeed.
quotes.context: REAL AUDIO candidate. Eye of the Storm (BBC 5 Live, 2019), file p07c6w6z approx 06:18-06:31 (small-model timing). ASR; confirm by ear.
reported_by: BBC Radio 5 Live Eye of the Storm, 2019, my transcript
quotes.korean: 엄빌리컬이 꽉 끼어 있었고, 그 반대편 끝에는 8천 톤짜리 배가 있었어요. 그 순간 저는 사실상 닻 역할을 하고 있었죠. 바로 그때 갑자기 깨달았어요. 상황이 정말 심각해졌다는 걸.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: He turned and tried desperately to get back towards me, arms flailing and we had this little moment where we were eyeball to eyeball looking in each other's eyes, before he was pulled backwards in to the darkness. Dave describes it like being in a film, which is exactly what it was like. He had this light on the top of his helmet and he was getting pulled back in to the darkness and we never saw each other again until it was all over…
quotes.context: The last sight of Dave Yuasa before the umbilical broke. First-person account published by OGV Energy, 27 Apr 2019. NOTE (CBC 2025): Lemons says they could NOT talk to each other at that point; the 2025 film's conversation is invented. Do not script any dialogue for Yuasa here.
quotes.korean: 데이브가 몸을 돌려 팔을 허우적대며 필사적으로 제게 오려 했어요. 그리고 아주 짧은 순간, 우리는 서로 눈을 똑바로 마주 봤죠. 그러고는 그가 뒤로, 어둠 속으로 끌려갔어요. 데이브는 영화 속 같았다고 하는데, 정말 딱 그랬어요. 헬멧 위 불빛을 단 채 어둠 속으로 끌려갔고, 모든 게 끝날 때까지 우린 다시 서로를 보지 못했어요…

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: When you see the Hollywood version, we have a bit of a chat, but in real life, we weren't able to talk to each other. I think my communication cable had been severed at that point. So we sort of had a face-to-face moment where I implored him to give me a hand and he basically looked me in the eye and said, you know, I can do nothing because he was restricted by the length of his own umbilical.
quotes.context: CBC The Current, 17 Mar 2025 (podscripts machine transcript). 'said, you know, I can do nothing' describes what Yuasa's LOOK conveyed; no words were spoken. Do not render as a Yuasa quote.
reported_by: CBC The Current podcast 17 Mar 2025 via podscripts.co transcript
quotes.korean: 할리우드 버전에선 둘이 대화를 좀 나누지만, 실제로는 서로 말을 할 수 없었어요. 그때 이미 통신 케이블이 끊어졌던 것 같아요. 그래서 얼굴을 마주한 채로, 저는 도와달라고 애원했고, 그는 제 눈을 보며, 말하자면 '아무것도 해줄 수 없다'는 눈빛이었어요. 그도 자기 엄빌리컬 길이에 묶여 있었으니까요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: It was like a jack being pulled from a speaker. I lost all communication, which puts you in a very lonely place. Then the hose, which provides an infinite amount of gas—suddenly I had nothing to breathe at all.
quotes.context: Losing comms and then the gas supply before the umbilical parted. Interview with Charles Digges, Nautilus, published 2 Oct 2025.
quotes.korean: 스피커에서 잭을 뽑아버린 것 같았어요. 교신이 전부 끊겼고, 그러면 정말 외로운 곳에 홀로 남게 되죠. 그다음은 호스였어요. 끝없이 가스를 대주던 그 호스에서, 갑자기 숨 쉴 게 하나도 나오지 않았어요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: First, the communications cable snapped. Then the gas hose stretched to the point I had nothing to breathe. I opened the supply on my back. This happened within about 30 seconds.
quotes.context: BBC Scotland News, 5 Apr 2019 (re-quoted by LADbible Jan 2025 with an editorial '[that]').
quotes.korean: 먼저 통신 케이블이 끊어졌어요. 다음엔 가스 호스가 늘어나서 숨 쉴 게 없어졌죠. 등에 멘 비상 가스를 열었어요. 이 모든 게 30초쯤 사이에 일어났어요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: Maybe 10 seconds after I turned that on, then my umbilical cord got to the point that it was so taut that it snapped with a really violent sort of shotgun sound and it, along with Dave, disappeared, sort of dragged backwards into the darkness and I was never to see them again really. So at that point suddenly I fell back to the seabed and in the most complete and absolute darkness basically.
quotes.context: REAL AUDIO candidate. Eye of the Storm (BBC 5 Live, released 4 Jun 2019), file p07c6w6z approx 07:27-07:52 (medium-model word timing). Good 6-8 s cuts: 07:31-07:44 ('it snapped... into the darkness') or 07:45-07:52 ('suddenly I fell back to the seabed... absolute darkness').
reported_by: BBC Radio 5 Live Eye of the Storm 2019, my transcript
quotes.korean: 그걸 켜고 10초쯤 지났을까, 엄빌리컬이 팽팽해질 대로 팽팽해지더니 끊어졌어요. 정말 격렬한, 산탄총 같은 소리와 함께요. 그리고 그 줄은 데이브와 함께 어둠 속으로 끌려가 사라졌고, 그 뒤로 다시는 그들을 보지 못했죠. 그 순간 저는 해저로 떨어졌어요. 그야말로 완전하고 절대적인 어둠 속으로요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: Soon after that the umbilical snapped like a shotgun going off and I fell down to the sea bed. Nearly 100m (approx 300ft) down in absolute darkness at two in the morning. I managed to find the structure we had been working on and found a way to climb up on top of that.
quotes.context: BBC Scotland News, 5 Apr 2019; '(approx 300ft)' is a BBC insertion. DISPUTE on the time of night: OGV 2019 has him saying 'It was 10pm at night' and 'We had only been diving for about an hour' (about 11pm), not 2am.
quotes.korean: 곧이어 엄빌리컬이 산탄총이 터지듯 끊어졌고, 저는 해저로 떨어졌어요. 수심 100미터 가까이, 새벽 두 시, 완전한 어둠 속이었어요. 작업하던 구조물을 겨우 찾아 그 위로 기어올랐죠.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: Yeah, instant. It was a flick of a switch [...] so I fell backwards onto the seabed which was about 10 or 11 meters below me. It was not just complete darkness instantaneously but complete silence. It was strange, yeah, suddenly a plunge from this world of panic and light to complete silence and darkness.
quotes.context: REAL AUDIO candidate, his own voice, BBC World Service Outlook (Emily Webb), 23 Apr 2019. File p0776q29 approx 17:47-18:06 (medium-model word timing); best 6-8 s cut about 17:53-18:06. ASR wording ('a plunge' vs 'you're plunged') must be checked by ear.
reported_by: BBC World Service Outlook podcast, 2019, my transcript
quotes.korean: 네, 한순간이었어요. 스위치를 탁 끈 것처럼요. […] 저는 10~11미터 아래 해저로 뒤로 넘어졌어요. 순식간에 완전한 어둠만 온 게 아니라, 완전한 침묵이 왔어요. 이상했죠. 공포와 빛의 세계에서 갑자기 완전한 침묵과 어둠 속으로 떨어진 거예요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: Suddenly I was falling backwards onto the seabed, in complete darkness. I had a gauge which told me how much gas I had but it was that dark I couldn't even see it. It was probably a good thing in retrospect, it would have been panic-inducing seeing how much I had left.
quotes.context: STV News, 'Last Breath: the diver who survived being lost at sea', 4 Apr 2019. Same idea in his own voice in Eye of the Storm (p07c6w6z approx 07:54-08:04) and Outlook (p0776q29 approx 22:12-22:22).
reported_by: BBC 5 Live / BBC World Service audio 2019
quotes.korean: 갑자기 뒤로 넘어지며 해저로 떨어졌어요. 완전한 어둠이었죠. 남은 가스량을 알려주는 게이지가 있었지만 너무 어두워서 보이지도 않았어요. 돌이켜보면 오히려 다행이었어요. 얼마 남았는지 봤다면 공황에 빠졌을 테니까요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: I fumbled around in the darkness and I was very lucky to bump into the structure. I could have very easily turned around and walked into no mans land. That was one of many doses of good fortune.
quotes.context: STV News, 4 Apr 2019. OGV 2019 version: 'I stumbled around in the darkness for a while and was very lucky to bump in to the structure, because I was completely disorientated.'
quotes.korean: 어둠 속을 더듬거리다가 운 좋게 구조물에 부딪혔어요. 자칫 엉뚱한 방향으로 돌아서 아무것도 없는 곳으로 걸어 들어갈 수도 있었어요. 그게 여러 번 찾아온 행운 중 하나였죠.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: ...climb to the top, fully expecting to see the lights of the diving bell somewhere above me and them trying to get back to me but there was absolutely nothing, nothing but darkness. And I think that's the point at which I thought this is not looking good.
quotes.context: REAL AUDIO candidate. Eye of the Storm (BBC 5 Live, 2019), file p07c6w6z approx 08:14-08:29 (medium timing). OGV 2019 text version: 'I quickly realised there was nothing, not a speck of light in the sea above me.'
reported_by: BBC Radio 5 Live Eye of the Storm 2019, my transcript
quotes.korean: …꼭대기로 올라갔어요. 머리 위 어딘가에 다이빙 벨 불빛이 보이고, 다들 저를 향해 돌아오고 있을 거라 굳게 믿으면서요. 그런데 정말 아무것도 없었어요. 어둠 말고는 아무것도. 그때 생각했죠. 이거 좋지 않다고.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: ...when I looked up into the sea above me and expecting to see the diving bell again and saw nothing, nothing, just blackness again, that I realised the chances of anybody getting to me in time were slim because it gives you enough time just to do a little bit of maths, you know, five minutes, I've probably used it for two or three, I've only got two left here, this is not going to end well at all.
quotes.context: REAL AUDIO candidate. BBC World Service Outlook, 23 Apr 2019, file p0776q29 approx 19:15-19:39 (medium timing). The next line 'I've got two minutes, I can't see anyone. I'm alone at the bottom of the North Sea' (19:41-19:50) is spoken by the PRESENTER, not Lemons.
reported_by: BBC World Service Outlook podcast 2019, my transcript
quotes.korean: …머리 위 바다를 올려다봤어요. 다이빙 벨이 다시 보일 거라 기대하면서요. 그런데 아무것도, 아무것도 없었어요. 또다시 새까만 어둠뿐. 그때 깨달았어요. 누군가 제때 저한테 닿을 가능성은 희박하다는 걸. 계산할 시간은 충분했거든요. 5분, 아마 2~3분은 썼고, 이제 2분 남았다. 이건 절대 좋게 끝나지 않겠구나.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: At that depth the bailout probably gives you around 5-6 minutes of gas and I'd already used about 2-3 minutes of this getting myself back up on the structure. Therefore, with no imminent signs of rescue or nowhere to go, you realise your chances of survival are pretty much zero.
quotes.context: Bailout arithmetic. OGV Energy, Apr 2019. Bailout duration is DISPUTED across sources, see notes (5 / 5-6 / 6 / 5-7 / 6-8 / 8-9 / 9-10 / 10 minutes).
quotes.korean: 그 수심에서 베일아웃은 아마 5~6분 정도 가스를 주는데, 구조물 위로 다시 올라가느라 벌써 2~3분을 써버렸어요. 구조될 기미도, 갈 곳도 없으니 살 가능성은 사실상 0이라는 걸 깨닫게 되죠.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: I realised very quickly that the end was nigh. I was on a countdown clock and it was counting very fast.
quotes.context: BBC Scotland News video 'North Sea diver's accident miracle' and article, Apr 2019. Same 'countdown clock' image in his own voice in Outlook (p0776q29 approx 22:22-22:26: 'what was effectively a countdown, a countdown clock to your death').
quotes.korean: 끝이 가까웠다는 걸 아주 빨리 깨달았어요. 저는 카운트다운 시계 위에 있었고, 그 시계는 아주 빠르게 줄어들고 있었어요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: The documentary makes a big deal of five minutes. The truth is I probably had about an eight or nine minute supply of gas on my back.
quotes.context: CBC The Current, 17 Mar 2025 (podscripts machine transcript; CBC article paraphrases it as 'eight or nine minutes'). His own later revision of the bailout figure. It contradicts his 2019 '5-6 minutes'.
reported_by: CBC The Current 2025 article and podscripts transcript
quotes.korean: 다큐멘터리는 '5분'을 크게 다루는데, 사실 제 등에는 아마 8~9분 정도 쓸 가스가 있었을 거예요.

quotes.speaker: Craig Frederick (dive supervisor)
quotes.words_en: Very aware. I mean, I make a calculation before every project and work out how much gas they've got for the depth they're working at. And the five minutes is a little bit lean. It was more between nine and 10 minutes, but five minutes is good enough. It depends on how quickly you breathe. But no, I was acutely aware that the clock was ticking for us to go effect a rescue.
quotes.context: REAL AUDIO candidate (supervisor's own voice). BBC World Service Outlook, 2019, file p0776q29 approx 23:42-24:04 (medium timing). The Independent 2019 reports his reckoning as 10 minutes ('Legally, he only needed five').
reported_by: BBC World Service Outlook podcast 2019, my transcript
quotes.korean: 아주 잘 알고 있었죠. 저는 작업 전마다 그 수심에서 다이버들이 가진 가스량을 계산해요. 5분은 좀 빠듯하게 잡은 거고, 실제로는 9분에서 10분 사이였어요. 그래도 5분이면 충분하다고 봐요. 호흡이 얼마나 빠르냐에 달렸으니까요. 아무튼 구조하러 갈 시간이 째깍째깍 흐르고 있다는 걸 뼈저리게 알고 있었어요.

quotes.speaker: Craig Frederick (dive supervisor)
quotes.words_en: All my monitors went dead so I had a completely different viewpoint than the divers. Normally I have lights and cameras and I had all that up until the point Chris's umbilical parted.
quotes.context: REAL AUDIO candidate. BBC World Service Outlook 2019, file p0776q29 approx 23:15-23:25.
reported_by: BBC World Service Outlook podcast 2019, my transcript
quotes.korean: 모니터가 전부 꺼졌어요. 그래서 다이버들과는 완전히 다른 시야에 놓였죠. 평소엔 조명도 카메라도 다 보이는데, 크리스의 엄빌리컬이 끊어진 그 순간까지만 보였어요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: I think once I accepted there was no hope of survival, I was powerless to do anything to save myself. A quiet resignation came over me. I remember it being a period of great sadness really, of disbelief. How I could find myself in this dark sad horrible place and this is where I would end my days. I thought of everybody at home and the chaos I would cause.
quotes.context: Acceptance on top of the manifold. BBC Scotland News, 5 Apr 2019.
quotes.korean: 살 가망이 없다는 걸 받아들이고 나니, 저 스스로를 구하려고 할 수 있는 건 아무것도 없었어요. 조용한 체념이 찾아왔죠. 정말 깊은 슬픔, 믿기지 않는 마음의 시간이었어요. 어쩌다 내가 이 어둡고 슬프고 끔찍한 곳에 와 있는 걸까, 여기서 생을 마치는구나. 집에 있는 모든 사람과, 제가 남기게 될 혼란을 생각했어요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: ...a calm, a resignation I think more than anything else comes over you so there was no wild panicking that I remember, no thrashing about, but just a real sadness I remember coming over me, washing over me, and thoughts of people at home and thoughts of the immense damage you're going to do to everybody you're leaving behind. [...] Yeah, it felt like a very lonely place to be. It was, as you say, very, very dark and utterly alone.
quotes.context: REAL AUDIO candidate. Eye of the Storm (BBC 5 Live, 2019), file p07c6w6z approx 09:03-09:20 and 09:27-09:33 (medium timing). Short cut: 09:27-09:33.
reported_by: BBC Radio 5 Live Eye of the Storm 2019, my transcript
quotes.korean: …무엇보다 고요함, 체념 같은 게 찾아와요. 미친 듯이 허우적댄 기억은 없어요. 그저 진짜 슬픔이 밀려와 저를 덮쳤던 게 기억나요. 집에 있는 사람들, 그리고 남겨두고 갈 모든 이에게 주게 될 엄청난 상처에 대한 생각이요. […] 네, 정말 외로운 곳이었어요. 말씀하신 대로 아주, 아주 어두웠고, 완전히 혼자였어요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: So I resigned myself quite quickly to the fact that this was probably going to be, sounds a bit silly now, but this is probably going to be the place that I die. But that had a strangely calming effect, I think, knowing that I couldn't do much to help myself.
quotes.context: CBC The Current, 17 Mar 2025 (podscripts transcript; CBC article prints 'That had a strangely calming effect, I think, knowing that I couldn't do much to help myself. I resigned myself quite quickly to the fact that this was probably going to be ... the place that I die.').
quotes.korean: 그래서 꽤 빨리 받아들였어요. 지금 말하면 좀 우습지만, 아마 여기가 내가 죽을 곳이구나 하고요. 그런데 그게 묘하게 마음을 가라앉혀 줬어요. 내가 나를 위해 할 수 있는 게 거의 없다는 걸 아니까요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: I can still feel how the fear drained out of me. I'd done all I could, and rather calmly thought, well, this is it—if this is how I have to go when my time comes, it really wasn't so bad.
quotes.context: Nautilus (Charles Digges), 2 Oct 2025.
quotes.korean: 두려움이 제 안에서 빠져나가던 느낌이 아직도 생생해요. 할 수 있는 건 다 했고, 꽤 담담하게 생각했어요. 그래, 이게 끝이구나. 언젠가 때가 왔을 때 이렇게 가는 거라면, 정말 그렇게 나쁘진 않았다고.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: I can remember actually calling out apologizing to her several times, you know, screaming up into the air, I was, you know, 'I'm so sorry, Morag, I'm so sorry.'
quotes.context: His fiancee Morag Martin. REAL AUDIO candidate, own voice, BBC World Service Outlook 2019, file p0776q29 approx 21:11-21:20 (ASR heard 'Maureen' = Morag; there is a pause or music after it). This settles the wording: Reader's Digest (2021) has '"I'm sorry, Morag!" he called out'; a 2019 review of the documentary has 'I am so sorry, Morag' as a thought. Use the Outlook wording.
reported_by: BBC World Service Outlook podcast 2019, my transcript
Reader's Digest, Simon Hemelryk, 29 Jul 2021 https://www.rd.com/?p=1641695
quotes.korean: 그녀에게 몇 번이나 사과하며 소리쳤던 게 기억나요. 허공을 향해 외쳤죠. '정말 미안해, 모라그. 정말 미안해.'

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: I was also calling for Duncan which was a strange thing and I think because he played this sort of father figure role and it would never have been him coming to fetch me anyway but I was for some reason I called his name out in some vain hope that he would drop out of nowhere and rescue me you know.
quotes.context: REAL AUDIO candidate. BBC World Service Outlook 2019, file p0776q29 approx 21:35-21:51 (medium timing). Reader's Digest 2021 version: 'He shouted out for Allcock. "Where are you?"' That is a reconstruction; prefer the Outlook audio.
reported_by: BBC World Service Outlook podcast 2019, my transcript
quotes.korean: 던컨도 불렀어요. 이상한 일이죠. 아마 그가 아버지 같은 존재였기 때문일 거예요. 어차피 저를 데리러 올 사람은 그가 아니었는데도, 왜인지 그의 이름을 외쳤어요. 그가 어디선가 불쑥 나타나 저를 구해줄 거라는 헛된 희망으로요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: I had all the hopes and dreams you have at that stage – of children, travel – and it felt as if all of that was about to be ripped away in this strange, lonely, ethereal place. [...] I grew up in a middle-class family on the outskirts of Cambridge, and I remember thinking: 'How is this dark, lonely place where I end my days?'
quotes.context: Interview with The Guardian (Sam Wollaston, about 7-8 Mar 2025, headline 'At the bottom of the North Sea, out of air and with no hope of rescue, I said goodbye to all my dreams'). The Guardian page is behind a bot challenge; text taken from LADbible (8 Mar 2025), which quotes the Guardian. CBC 2025 audio version: 'I grew up in a sort of middle class family in Cambridge, you know, how have I ended up dying in this dark lonely place?'
reported_by: LADbible, Anish Vij, 8 Mar 2025, quoting The Guardian https://www.ladbible.com/news/uk-news/chris-lemons-diver-stuck-bottom-ocean-516495-20250308
quotes.korean: 그 나이 때 누구나 품는 희망과 꿈이 있었어요. 아이, 여행… 그 모든 게 이 낯설고, 외롭고, 이 세상 같지 않은 곳에서 막 뜯겨 나가려는 것 같았죠. […] 케임브리지 외곽의 평범한 중산층 집에서 자랐는데, 그런 생각이 들었던 게 기억나요. '이 어둡고 외로운 곳이 내 생이 끝나는 곳이라니.'

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: Suddenly you're there about to die in the depth and the darkness of the North Sea.
quotes.context: STV News, 4 Apr 2019.
quotes.korean: 갑자기, 북해의 깊고 어두운 곳에서 죽기 직전인 거예요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: It seemed like the most hopeless possible situation, and I very much resigned myself to what I felt was absolutely certain death.
quotes.context: PEOPLE magazine, 2025 (read via AOL syndication 'Is Last Breath a True Story?', Keith Langston, 4 Mar 2025). Caution: that article wrongly puts supervisor Craig Frederick in the bell; Allcock was the bellman.
quotes.korean: 더 이상 절망적일 수 없는 상황 같았고, 저는 확실한 죽음이라고 느낀 그것을 완전히 받아들였어요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: When you're sort of in the last vestiges of helium in the tank you can definitely feel it get a little bit tighter, it's a little bit harder to suck it down and that was a moment which took a lot longer to come than I thought it would. [...] But when it did come, there was a definite realization that, you know, this was it, and I really hope it doesn't hurt.
quotes.context: REAL AUDIO candidate. BBC World Service Outlook 2019, file p0776q29 approx 22:00-22:32 (medium timing). Short cut: 22:27-22:32.
reported_by: BBC World Service Outlook podcast 2019, my transcript
quotes.korean: 탱크에 헬륨이 마지막으로 조금 남았을 때는 확실히 느껴져요. 조금씩 빡빡해지고, 들이마시기가 조금씩 힘들어지죠. 그 순간은 생각보다 훨씬 늦게 왔어요. […] 하지만 막상 오니까, 분명히 깨달았어요. 아, 이게 끝이구나. 제발 아프지 않았으면.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: No. When you think about going to sleep last night, you can probably remember getting drowsy and, you know, counting sheep or whatever it is, but you don't remember that exact moment of slipping into unconsciousness effectively, and it was very much the same, yeah. So it wasn't an unpleasant finale, if you like. But yeah, no real memory of the very last moment.
quotes.context: Answer to 'Do you remember losing consciousness?'. BBC World Service Outlook 2019, file p0776q29 approx 22:39-22:59. CBC 2025 version: 'I remember the gas getting a bit harder to breathe so I knew I was running out, but I don't remember those very final moments... If that's how I go in the end, that wasn't awful.'
reported_by: BBC World Service Outlook podcast 2019, my transcript
quotes.korean: 아뇨. 어젯밤 잠들 때를 떠올려 보면, 졸음이 오고 양을 세고 그런 건 기억나도, 정확히 의식이 끊기는 그 순간은 기억 못 하잖아요. 딱 그랬어요. 그러니 불쾌한 마지막은 아니었어요. 하지만 정말 마지막 순간은 기억에 없어요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: I'd like to think I controlled my breathing and calmed myself and that's what I... curled up in a little ball, sort of fetus-like on the top of this structure and waited for it all to end... I'd like to think maybe six, seven, eight, nine minutes possibly before I actually fell unconscious.
quotes.context: Eye of the Storm (BBC 5 Live 2019), file p07c6w6z approx 10:54-11:16 (small-model timing; ASR). CBC 2025: 'I pretty much assumed the fetal position in the middle of the structure on the roof and tried to put myself in the best place to be found.'
reported_by: BBC Radio 5 Live Eye of the Storm 2019, my transcript
quotes.korean: 호흡을 다스리고 마음을 가라앉혔다고 믿고 싶어요. 구조물 꼭대기에서 태아처럼 작게 웅크린 채, 모든 게 끝나기를 기다렸죠… 실제로 의식을 잃기까지 6, 7, 8, 9분쯤 걸리지 않았을까 싶어요.

quotes.speaker: Craig Frederick (dive supervisor)
quotes.words_en: challenge was not to give [Allcock and Yuasa] too much information. It looked pretty hopeless, as far as they were concerned, so I couldn't tell them we were 250m from Chris and we hadn't gained control of the ship. So, essentially, I took it on myself to gee them up and say, 'Yes, we're making progress. We're going to get it back there. I have total confidence this isn't a recovery mission, it's a rescue mission'.
quotes.context: During the roughly 20-30 minutes the ship was out of control. The Independent, Stephen Applebaum, 15 Apr 2019 (via Yahoo). The first words are partly in the journalist's framing ('Frederick says his "challenge was..."'). The quoted lines to the divers are his recollection.
quotes.korean: (제 과제는) 그들에게 너무 많은 정보를 주지 않는 거였어요. 그들 입장에선 꽤 절망적으로 보였을 테니까요. 우리가 크리스에게서 250미터 떨어져 있고 아직 배를 통제하지 못했다고는 말할 수 없었어요. 그래서 제가 나서서 기운을 북돋웠죠. '그래, 진전이 있어. 다시 거기로 갈 거야. 확신한다. 이건 시신 수습이 아니라 구조 작전이야.'

quotes.speaker: Craig Frederick (dive supervisor)
quotes.words_en: I was under the spotlight but I wasn't going to relinquish control of the dive to anyone else. It was certainly my responsibility.
quotes.context: REAL AUDIO candidate. BBC World Service Outlook 2019, file p0776q29 approx 25:20-25:28. In the same interview: regained control after 'maybe 20 minutes', drifted 'maybe 250 metres' (24:59-25:11); ship back on site and Dave down 'I would say 35 minutes probably' (26:45-26:49).
reported_by: BBC World Service Outlook podcast 2019, my transcript
quotes.korean: 모든 시선이 제게 쏠려 있었지만, 이 잠수의 지휘권을 누구에게도 넘길 생각은 없었어요. 분명히 제 책임이었으니까요.

quotes.speaker: Craig Frederick (dive supervisor)
quotes.words_en: I wanted to see that it was severed rather than it pulled off his harness and we ended up with his hat. As long as he had his diving helmet, then he had a good chance of surviving.
quotes.context: Why he told Allcock to pull the broken umbilical into the bell. The Independent, 15 Apr 2019.
quotes.korean: 줄이 끊어진 건지, 아니면 하네스에서 빠져서 헬멧까지 딸려 올라온 건지 확인하고 싶었어요. 헬멧만 쓰고 있다면 살 가능성이 충분했으니까요.

quotes.speaker: Dave Yuasa
quotes.words_en: [He watched Lemons's umbilical] getting thin, which I'd never seen before. [...] quite a lot of tearing, which would have been the other ones parting, one by one. That was quite memorable, actually.
quotes.context: Yuasa, within a metre of Lemons, watching the umbilical stretch and break. Fragments only, embedded in the journalist's sentences (he 'heard a bang, which he assumes was the "armour-plated" cable snapping'). The Independent, Stephen Applebaum, 15 Apr 2019.
quotes.korean: (엄빌리컬이) 가늘어지는 게 보였어요. 처음 보는 광경이었죠. […] 찢어지는 소리가 꽤 많이 났어요. 나머지 호스들이 하나씩 끊어지는 소리였겠죠. 사실 꽤 기억에 남아요.

quotes.speaker: Dave Yuasa
quotes.words_en: It was quite a long ride. I was kind of in mid-water. So, I made my way back to the bell, which was a physical effort, but it was the only place I could have gone anyway, really.
quotes.context: Being dragged away with the bell. The Independent, 15 Apr 2019. The National (25 Jun 2019, same author) adds: 'I was getting pulled through the water, and was a little bit worried that there could be some trouble coming for me as well, because there were other things down there that could have caught me up.'
quotes.korean: 꽤 긴 '드라이브'였어요. 거의 물 한가운데 떠 있었죠. 그래서 벨로 돌아갔어요. 몸은 힘들었지만, 어차피 갈 수 있는 곳은 거기밖에 없었으니까요.

quotes.speaker: Dave Yuasa
quotes.words_en: I think you're meant to have a minute of breathing gas for every 10 metres of umbilical cable that you've got, and that's enough to get you back to the bell, and no more. I didn't have a watch on, but I knew it had been a lot more than five minutes. So I thought he was definitely going to be dead. I just hoped it was quick and that it hadn't hurt.
quotes.context: Waiting under the bell while the ship was out of control. The National, 25 Jun 2019 (the journalist adds '[they had 50 metres]'). The Independent version: 'I was thinking, "I hope it doesn't hurt. I hope it's quick." It's a bad death, isn't it? For a start, you're alone. So I hoped it was quick and that it hadn't hurt. And I was glad it wasn't me.'
quotes.korean: 엄빌리컬 10미터당 호흡 가스 1분이 있어야 한다고들 해요. 벨까지 돌아갈 수 있을 만큼, 딱 그만큼이요. 시계는 안 차고 있었지만, 5분은 훨씬 넘었다는 걸 알았어요. 그래서 그는 분명 죽었을 거라고 생각했죠. 그저 빨리, 아프지 않게 끝났기만을 바랐어요.

quotes.speaker: Dave Yuasa
quotes.words_en: I didn't expect him to be alive. Why would you?
quotes.context: On reaching Lemons on top of the structure once the ship was back on station. The Independent, 15 Apr 2019. Lemons (Eye of the Storm 2019) paraphrases Dave as treating it 'as coming to rescue a dead body, a dead weight'. That is a paraphrase, not Dave's words.
quotes.korean: 살아 있을 거라곤 기대하지 않았어요. 누가 그러겠어요?

quotes.speaker: Dave Yuasa
quotes.words_en: When he turned out to be OK it was a massive relief, if somewhat anticlimactic.
quotes.context: The Independent, 15 Apr 2019 (The National's version ends at 'massive relief'). The preceding sentence about being 'stuck in the chamber with a dead body for three days' is blunt; use with care.
quotes.korean: 그가 괜찮다는 게 밝혀졌을 때, 엄청나게 안도했어요. 조금 김이 빠지긴 했지만요.

quotes.speaker: Dave Yuasa
quotes.words_en: It's safe as long as everything goes right. And if it goes wrong, it's instantly dangerous.
quotes.context: On saturation diving in general. The Independent 15 Apr 2019 and The National 25 Jun 2019.
quotes.korean: 모든 게 제대로 돌아가는 동안엔 안전해요. 하지만 하나라도 잘못되면, 그 즉시 위험해지죠.

quotes.speaker: Duncan Allcock
quotes.words_en: It was so tight. There was no way I could even get my fingers in to pull [more umbilical] off, let alone pull it over the top of the horns where it's wrapped up ... It was literally pulling the rack, which is like four-inch stainless-steel bars, off the wall. For a moment I thought it was going to pull me out of the hole to them. I literally jumped on the chair at the opposite side of the bell, and pinned myself to the roof, like Spider-Man, just trying to get out of the way.
quotes.context: Allcock was the bellman, inside the bell. The Independent, Stephen Applebaum, 15 Apr 2019. Frederick confirms in Outlook audio that Duncan 'was trying to make himself as small as possible'.
quotes.korean: 너무 팽팽했어요. 줄을 더 풀어주려고 손가락 하나 넣을 틈도 없었죠. 감긴 걸 걸이 위로 넘기는 건 말할 것도 없고요… 말 그대로 4인치짜리 스테인리스 봉으로 된 랙을 벽에서 뜯어내고 있었어요. 한순간 저까지 그 구멍 밖으로, 그들 쪽으로 끌려 나가겠구나 싶었어요. 벨 반대편 의자로 뛰어올라 스파이더맨처럼 천장에 몸을 붙였죠. 그냥 피하려고요.

quotes.speaker: Duncan Allcock
quotes.words_en: I knew in my heart of hearts, when I started pulling his umbilical in, that he wasn't on the end. But until I got both hoses in my hand, one by one, I literally felt sick.
quotes.context: Pulling in the severed umbilical. The Independent, 15 Apr 2019. The sentence before it, 'didn't know whether to spew, shit, or cry', is crude; leave it out. The same piece reports that turning off his friend's gas 'felt like I was killing him' (fragment).
quotes.korean: 그의 엄빌리컬을 끌어올리기 시작했을 때, 마음 깊은 곳에선 알았어요. 그 끝에 그가 없다는 걸. 그래도 호스 두 개를 하나씩 손에 쥐기 전까지는… 정말 속이 메스꺼웠어요.

quotes.speaker: Duncan Allcock
quotes.words_en: I've lost my diver! I've lost my diver!
quotes.context: Shouted in the bell on 18 Sep 2012 when the broken hoses came up; recorded on the comms and heard in the 2019 documentary. That audio is documentary footage: do NOT use it. Wording varies: STV 4 Apr 2019 'I've lost my diver, I've lost my diver!'; a 2019 review 'I've lost me diver! I've lost me diver!'; Reader's Digest 2021 'I've lost my diver!' shouted to Frederick.
quotes.korean: 다이버를 잃었어! 내 다이버를 잃었어!

quotes.speaker: Duncan Allcock
quotes.words_en: He's a bald guy, he's half frozen to death, and he's gone as blue as a pair of denim jeans.
quotes.context: Removing Lemons's helmet in the bell. The Independent, 15 Apr 2019. Frederick's Outlook recollection of Allcock on the intercom: 'I got his hat off, he's really blue' (p0776q29 approx 27:40-27:43).
quotes.korean: 대머리인 친구가 반쯤 얼어 죽어서는, 청바지처럼 새파랗게 질려 있었어요.

quotes.speaker: Duncan Allcock
quotes.words_en: Chris took one of those sorts of breath [demonstrates a sharp gulp of air] – which to me was like New Year, crackers, fireworks, you name it. Everything. It was like, 'Bloody hell! He's actually alive!'
quotes.context: After the rescue breaths in the bell. The Independent, 15 Apr 2019.
quotes.korean: 크리스가 '헉' 하고 숨을 들이켰는데, 저한텐 새해 같았어요. 폭죽, 불꽃놀이, 뭐든지요. 전부 다요. '세상에! 진짜 살아 있잖아!' 그런 기분이었죠.

quotes.speaker: Craig Frederick (dive supervisor)
quotes.words_en: Well I get goose bumps now talking about it and even thinking about it. He just said look he's alive, he's breathing, he's actually talking and it was remarkable.
quotes.context: REAL AUDIO candidate. Frederick quoting what Allcock told him over the bell intercom. BBC World Service Outlook 2019, file p0776q29 approx 28:04-28:16 (medium timing).
reported_by: BBC World Service Outlook podcast 2019, my transcript
quotes.korean: 지금도 그 얘길 하거나 떠올리기만 해도 소름이 돋아요. 던컨이 그냥 '봐, 살아 있어, 숨 쉬고 있어, 말까지 해' 하더라고요. 정말 놀라웠어요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: Duncan, who was in there, rips my diving helmet off and he said that my head was extraordinarily blue, sort of bright, bright blue. And he, I think more in hope than expectation, just put his lips to mine and gave me a good couple of breaths and apparently I came to almost straight away, a gasp and a cough and I came around immediately, which I think everybody was pretty astonished at.
quotes.context: REAL AUDIO candidate. Eye of the Storm (BBC 5 Live 2019), file p07c6w6z approx 13:59-14:23 (ASR said 'hope of an expectation'). OGV 2019 text: 'Duncan who was in there too, ripped my helmet off and gave me two breaths and amazingly, I came round almost immediately. I gasped then essentially came back to life.'
reported_by: BBC Radio 5 Live Eye of the Storm 2019, my transcript
quotes.korean: 벨 안에 있던 던컨이 제 헬멧을 확 벗겼는데, 제 머리가 엄청나게 파랬대요. 새파랗게요. 그리고 기대보다는 희망을 품고 제 입에 입을 대고 숨을 두어 번 불어넣었어요. 그랬더니 거의 곧바로 깨어났대요. 헉 하고 숨을 들이켜고, 기침하고, 바로 정신이 돌아왔죠. 다들 꽤 놀랐던 것 같아요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: I have a recollection of seeing Dave, in fact, crumpled on the other side of the bell, exhausted and thinking, you know, what's wrong with him? He looks awfully tired, yeah. So I think I reached out and I grabbed Duncan's hand at some point, so I obviously realised something had happened and gave it a squeeze.
quotes.context: Waking in the bell. REAL AUDIO candidate, Eye of the Storm (BBC 5 Live 2019), file p07c6w6z approx 15:03-15:23 (medium timing).
reported_by: BBC Radio 5 Live Eye of the Storm 2019, my transcript
quotes.korean: 벨 반대편에 데이브가 녹초가 되어 쓰러져 있던 게 기억나요. 그러면서 생각했죠. '쟤 왜 저래? 엄청 피곤해 보이네.' 그러다 어느 순간 손을 뻗어 던컨의 손을 잡았던 것 같아요. 무슨 일이 있었다는 건 알았던 거죠. 그 손을 꼭 쥐었어요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: I didn't see any bright, beckoning lights when I was out. When I came to in the bell, I was confused, though I understood from the expressions on Dave [Yuasa] and Duncan's [Allcock's] faces that something serious had happened. But it would be a while before I connected it to myself.
quotes.context: Nautilus (Charles Digges), 2 Oct 2025.
quotes.korean: 의식을 잃은 동안 저를 부르는 밝은 빛 같은 건 보지 못했어요. 벨 안에서 깨어났을 때는 혼란스러웠어요. 데이브와 던컨의 표정을 보고 뭔가 심각한 일이 있었다는 건 알았지만, 그게 저에게 일어난 일이라는 걸 연결 짓기까지는 한참 걸렸어요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: They're the real heroes in this story. And everyone on the boat. I'm just a damsel in distress.
quotes.context: About Yuasa and Allcock. Guardian interview (Sam Wollaston, Mar 2025) as quoted by LADbible 8 Mar 2025. He also says 'I'm absolutely the damsel in distress at that point' on CBC 2025.
quotes.korean: 그들이 이 이야기의 진짜 영웅이에요. 배에 있던 모든 사람도요. 저는 그냥 구해지길 기다린 '곤경에 빠진 공주'였을 뿐이고요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: Dave came down and put in a super-human effort to drag me back to the bell. He is a really fit guy and even he struggled pulling the weight of my body back to the bell.
quotes.context: OGV Energy, Apr 2019. CBC 2025: 'A superhuman effort that I can obviously never thank him for, enough for anyway.'
quotes.korean: 데이브가 내려와서 초인적인 힘으로 저를 벨까지 끌고 갔어요. 정말 체력 좋은 친구인데도, 제 몸무게를 벨까지 끌어올리느라 애를 먹었죠.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: I think it was a case of getting back on the bike a little bit and if we perhaps we hadn't gone back then maybe we we never would have, I don't know. We were nervous but not in a bad way, there was a lot of nervous laughter and so on but it was strange, I think as soon as we got into the water the same three, you know, it was Duncan, Dave and myself, we all went back together to the same place. Once we were back in the water and back on a job it's incredible how quickly you forget things.
quotes.context: Going back to diving. REAL AUDIO candidate, BBC World Service Outlook 2019, file p0776q29 approx 33:40-34:06 (medium timing). Same in Eye of the Storm approx 18:21-18:33.
reported_by: BBC World Service Outlook podcast 2019, my transcript
BBC Radio 5 Live Eye of the Storm 2019
quotes.korean: 다시 자전거에 올라타는 것 같은 거였어요. 그때 돌아가지 않았다면 영영 못 돌아갔을지도 몰라요. 긴장했지만 나쁜 쪽은 아니었어요. 어색한 웃음이 많았죠. 그런데 신기하게도, 물에 들어가자마자 똑같은 셋이, 던컨, 데이브, 그리고 제가 다 함께 그 같은 장소로 돌아갔어요. 다시 물속에서 일을 하다 보면, 얼마나 빨리 잊게 되는지 놀라울 정도예요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: We went back to the very same place because my umbilical was caught that night on a transponder bucket, which is like a metal outcrop, and that shouldn't have been there. So it was straight back to the scene of the crime.
quotes.context: PEOPLE 2025 (via AOL). CBC 2025: 'we went back three weeks later to the same place where we were the first people back in the water.' Reader's Digest 2021: 'I didn't want to lose my nerve.'
quotes.korean: 저흰 바로 그 장소로 돌아갔어요. 그날 밤 제 엄빌리컬이 걸린 건 트랜스폰더 버킷이라는, 툭 튀어나온 금속 구조물이었는데, 원래 거기 있으면 안 되는 거였거든요. 그러니 곧장 '사건 현장'으로 돌아간 셈이죠.

quotes.speaker: Duncan Allcock
quotes.words_en: I'm proud of him. Many would have said, 'This is too dangerous. I'm not coming back.'
quotes.context: On Lemons returning to dive three weeks later. Reader's Digest, Simon Hemelryk, 29 Jul 2021 (interview-based narrative).
quotes.korean: 그가 자랑스러워요. 많은 사람이 '너무 위험해. 다신 안 돌아가'라고 했을 거예요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: I've had a glimpse of dying and I'm not scared. I know I'm lucky to have a second chance. I always had a lust for life, and the accident only made that stronger.
quotes.context: Reader's Digest, 2021.
quotes.korean: 죽음을 살짝 엿봤는데, 두렵지 않아요. 두 번째 기회를 얻은 게 행운이라는 걸 알아요. 늘 삶에 대한 열망이 컸는데, 그 사고가 그걸 더 강하게 만들었을 뿐이에요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: I feel like a bit of a charlatan. I still get contacted all the time by people who've lost loved ones, but I don't have the right to tell you what it's like – I didn't die.
quotes.context: Guardian 2025 via LADbible 8 Mar 2025. Similar wording on GB News 15 Mar 2025 and CBC 2025.
quotes.korean: 제가 좀 사기꾼 같다는 기분이 들어요. 사랑하는 사람을 잃은 분들이 지금도 계속 연락을 주시는데, 저는 그게 어떤 건지 말할 자격이 없어요. 저는 죽지 않았으니까요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: The people who suffer are not really the three of us who can affect the outcome, it's the people you leave at home — your family, your friends, the ones who have to sit at home and imagine the worst.
quotes.context: Business Insider (Britney Nguyen), 26 Nov 2022, via Yahoo syndication.
quotes.korean: 정말 고통받는 건 결과를 바꿀 수 있는 저희 셋이 아니에요. 집에 남은 사람들이죠. 가족, 친구들. 집에 앉아서 최악을 상상해야 하는 사람들이요.

quotes.speaker: Morag Martin (Lemons's then-fiancee, now wife)
quotes.words_en: My stomach still churns to hear the story. I came ridiculously close to losing him and being robbed of the life we were going to have. I'm extremely grateful to both of them.
quotes.context: About Yuasa and Allcock. BBC Scotland News, 5 Apr 2019.
quotes.korean: 그 이야기를 들으면 아직도 속이 뒤틀려요. 그를 잃고, 우리가 함께 살아갈 삶을 빼앗길 뻔했어요. 말도 안 될 만큼 가까이요. 두 사람에게 정말 깊이 감사해요.

quotes.speaker: Craig Frederick (dive supervisor)
quotes.words_en: It meant his blood was saturated with oxygen. And the cold helped him because the brain was going to shut down all the other bits before it shut itself down. And he didn't actually drown. He just stopped breathing. But how he survived, I'll never know for sure.
quotes.context: The National (Stephen Applebaum), 25 Jun 2019. He links it to the high oxygen content of that day's bailout gas.
quotes.korean: 그의 혈액이 산소로 포화돼 있었다는 뜻이죠. 그리고 추위가 도왔어요. 뇌가 스스로 멈추기 전에 다른 부분들을 먼저 꺼버렸을 테니까요. 그리고 그는 익사한 게 아니에요. 그냥 숨이 멎었던 거죠. 하지만 그가 어떻게 살아났는지는, 저도 끝내 확실히는 모를 거예요.

quotes.speaker: Jochen Schipke (retired physiology professor, co-author of a case report on Lemons)
quotes.words_en: This was close to perfection. Not so much luck. This was training. This was knowledge. This was experience.
quotes.context: CBC The Current web article, 22 Mar 2025.
quotes.korean: 완벽에 가까웠어요. 운이라기보다는요. 훈련이었고, 지식이었고, 경험이었어요.

quotes.speaker: Chris Lemons
quotes.words_en: I'd like to offer my sincere thanks to all those people locally who have shown me such kindness since my return - it has been more than a little overwhelming.
quotes.context: Earliest quote found, Oct 2012, local Morar/Mallaig paper West Word. CAUTION: the same 2012 article contains errors (bailout 'about 15 minutes', 'the bellman slapped him', 'over 260 feet', '25 minutes').
quotes.korean: 돌아온 뒤로 따뜻한 마음을 보여주신 동네 모든 분께 진심으로 감사드립니다. 솔직히 감당하기 벅찰 만큼이었어요.

quotes.notes:
I collected 60 quotes. Three BBC/CBC interviews give real-audio clips in Lemons's own voice, and the BBC Outlook episode also has supervisor Craig Frederick's own voice. I found no recording of Dave Yuasa or Duncan Allcock outside the documentary, so their words can appear only as on-screen text.

AUDIO (own voices, not the documentary):
1. BBC World Service Outlook, 'How did this diver cheat death?', Emily Webb, 23 Apr 2019. Podcast version p0776q29, 2140 s, with Lemons and Frederick. It downloaded directly from open.live.bbc.co.uk/mediaselector/6/redir/version/2.0/mediaset/audio-nondrm-download/proto/https/vpid/p0776q29.mp3. The presenter says it includes 'recordings from the day' supplied by Dogwoof (documentary or comms audio, around 10:39-10:45 and possibly near 14:34-14:40 and 15:13-15:39). Do not use those parts.
2. BBC Radio 5 Live 'Eye of the Storm', Emma Barnett, 'Diver who cheated death', released 4 Jun 2019. Podcast version p07c6w6z, 1327 s, Lemons only. It opens with a documentary clip at about 00:46-01:26; do not use it.
3. CBC The Current, Matt Galloway, 17 Mar 2025. I have only the podscripts.co transcript; I could not get the audio. The page points to akamai 'prodAudio/radio/2025/03/17/dave-yURXXcG5-20250317.mp3', but that path did not resolve, and the RSS feed only goes back to Nov 2025.
4. The Big Interview ep 19 (Omny, 31 Jan 2021) is downloaded to lq_audio/bigint.mp3 but not transcribed. Other podcasts I found but did not fetch: The You Project 679, Roll With The Punches ep242 (both have Omny audio URLs), Against the Odds 'In Their Own Words', Pretty Sure I Can Fly, Big Scuba Podcast ep163.
YouTube was not tried.

Every timestamp is in the podcast files listed above. The wording comes from my faster-whisper transcripts (small model for whole episodes, medium model for the key windows), so check each clip by ear before subtitling. One line that sounds like Lemons is not: 'I've got two minutes, I can't see anyone. I'm alone at the bottom of the North Sea' (Outlook about 19:41-19:50) is the presenter.

Files, all in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aireels/82e206d8-83ed-5019-be3d-65c96a1bf62c/scratchpad:
- lq_audio/p0776q29.audio-nondrm-download.mp3 and lq_audio/p07c6w6z.audio-nondrm-download.mp3 (full quality)
- lq_audio/p0776q29.16k.wav.small.txt and lq_audio/p07c6w6z.16k.wav.small.txt (full transcripts)
- lq_audio/wins_medium.txt (key windows with word-level timestamps)
- lq/podscripts.txt (CBC transcript)

DISPUTES TO FLAG:
- **Depth.** 2012 local paper: 'over 260 ft' (about 80 m); a search snippet of a 2012 Energy Voice report gave '262ft', unread because the page is blocked. BBC 2012: '300ft'. BBC 2019: bell 'lowered 91m' but also 'almost 100m'. Lemons gives 'about 90m' (GB News 2025) and 'ship 90 m above us' (Eye of the Storm), and 'nearly a hundred meters' (CBC). The chamber was pressurised to 100 m. The structure was about 10-11 m high, which may explain the 90-100 m spread.
- **Bailout gas.** Documentary and Wikipedia: 5 min. BBC 2019 and Outlook: 5-6 (the BBC article also says 'six-minute emergency air tank'). Eye of the Storm: 5-7. GB News 2025: 6-8. CBC 2025: 8-9 ('The documentary makes a big deal of five minutes'). Frederick: 9-10 (Outlook) or 10 (Independent). The 2012 local paper says 15, which looks wrong.
- **Time without gas, or until rescue.** About 25 min: 2012 paper, Eye of the Storm 'best guess', CBC episode title. About 30: many sources. 30-35: GB News and Outlook. 35: BBC 2019 says 35 minutes after he turned on the bailout; Frederick says 'I would say 35 minutes'. CBC 2025: 'nearly 35, 36 minutes... since I've run out' of gas. 38: Undercurrent and Business Insider NL. 'Nearly 40' or 'over 40' until rescue: GB News 2025, Divernet, speaker bios. Keep apart the time since the umbilical broke (about 35-40 min) and the time with no gas (about 25-30+ min).
- **Getting the ship back.** Frederick: control regained after 'maybe 20 minutes', ship drifted 'maybe 250 metres'. Lemons: 'nearly 30 minutes' (OGV), the ship 'nearly 200 meters' away (Eye of the Storm), 'nearly a thousand feet' (CBC).
- **Time of night.** BBC 2019 quotes him saying 'two in the morning'. OGV 2019 has '10pm... only been diving for about an hour'.
- **Rescue breaths.** Allcock gave them: 'two rescue breaths' or 'a good couple of breaths'. Some content farms wrongly credit Yuasa, and the 2012 paper says the bellman 'slapped him'. PEOPLE wrongly puts Frederick in the bell; he was in dive control on the ship.
- **Bailout equipment.** It was open-circuit scuba cylinders. Undercurrent's 'closed-circuit rebreather' is wrong; the COBRA rebreather was introduced afterwards (OGV).
- **Misspoken date.** In Eye of the Storm Lemons says 'this happened in November'. The date was 18 Sep 2012.

OTHER CAUTIONS:
- Lemons says he and Yuasa could not speak on the seabed; the 2025 film's dialogue between them is invented. Do not script any words for Yuasa there.
- Allcock's shout 'I've lost my diver!' exists only in the documentary's comms audio, so it can be text only.
- The Guardian 2025 article (Sam Wollaston) is behind a bot challenge, which I did not get around; its quotes come via LADbible.
- Several Yuasa and Allcock lines are blunt or crude: 'glad it wasn't me', 'dead body for three days', 'spew, shit, or cry'. Use with care.
