- Outlook also has gentler lines not listed above, for the ending: Lemons's wedding-speech thanks to Allcock for 'a decent kiss on the lips' (about 33:06-33:12), Morag meeting him on the gangplank (about 32:10-32:18), and Frederick asking 'Chris, how are you doing? Everything okay?' (about 29:05-29:15).
- The Korean lines are faithful, natural spoken translations; brackets mark cuts or editorial insertions.

Key text sources: BBC Scotland 5 Apr 2019 (Debbie Jackson); The Independent 15 Apr 2019 (Stephen Applebaum, read via Yahoo); The National 25 Jun 2019; OGV Energy Apr 2019; STV 4 Apr 2019; CBC 22 Mar 2025; Nautilus 2 Oct 2025; PEOPLE via AOL Mar 2025; Reader's Digest 2021; Business Insider 2022; GB News 15 Mar 2025; LADbible (quoting the Guardian) 8 Mar 2025; BBC 25 Sep 2012; West Word Oct 2012.

clips.speaker: Chris Lemons
clips.words_en: suddenly a plunge from this world of panic and light to complete silence and darkness
clips.notes: BEST darkness clip, studio quality. A low BBC music drone fades in under the last word from about 1070.7 s. Cut at 1070.95 with a short fade. From 1071.3 s the music is fully up.

clips.speaker: Chris Lemons
clips.words_en: it was not just complete darkness instantaneously but complete silence instantaneous(ly). It was, it was strange
clips.notes: Clean, with no music. Alternative to or lead-in for the clip above (1059.6-1070.95 together is 11.3 s).

clips.speaker: Chris Lemons
clips.words_en: instant, it was a flick of a switch, actually released the tension, so I fell backwards onto the seabed which was about 10 or 11 meters below me
clips.notes: Answer to the host's question 'were you plunged into darkness?'. Starting at 1051.95 includes 'yeah', but the host's question tail may sit just before it, so start at 1052.2. Clean.

clips.speaker: Chris Lemons
clips.words_en: when I looked up into the sea above me expecting to see the diving bell again and saw nothing, nothing, just blackness
clips.notes: Climbing onto the manifold in darkness. Room tone in the pauses is around -40 dB and noise-like, with no tonal music. End after 'blackness'; the next word 'again' starts at 1150.3.

clips.speaker: Chris Lemons
clips.words_en: five minutes, I've probably used it for two or three, I've only got two left here, this is, this is not going to end well at all
clips.notes: Bailout running out, as he reasoned at the time (his own estimate of 5 minutes). Clean.

clips.speaker: Chris Lemons
clips.words_en: The maths tell us that I would have had, at that depth, five to six minutes of gas, yeah.
clips.notes: Bailout duration in his words. DISPUTED: the dive supervisor in the same episode says 9-10 minutes (see 1416.3).

clips.speaker: Chris Lemons
clips.words_en: I ran out of gas very quickly. Suddenly it came upon me. I think the gas hose had stretched to the point that it was crimped and I wasn't getting any supply down it.
clips.notes: Main gas lost before the snap. Use the short version 985.45-988.4 ('I ran out of gas very quickly. Suddenly it came upon me.'). Clean.

clips.speaker: Chris Lemons
clips.words_en: Then there was this outrageous shotgun bang
clips.notes: The BBC added a bang SFX followed by music starting at about 1020.75 (loud, tonal through to 1043). Hard-cut at 1020.7 or earlier. Do not use 1020.75-1043.

clips.speaker: Chris Lemons
clips.words_en: the sort of weight of 8,000 tons of boat was pulling it so tight so quickly that I was completely powerless to do anything about it really
clips.notes: Umbilical snagged on the transponder bucket. Clean, studio quality.

clips.speaker: Chris Lemons
clips.words_en: that's the point at which I realised I was in serious, serious trouble. I knew immediately this was going to be... life-threatening
clips.notes: Clean.

clips.speaker: Chris Lemons
clips.words_en: He was actually bending the sort of stainless steel rack off the wall of the diving bell, it was so tight
clips.notes: About Duncan Allcock in the bell. The presenter's narration ends at 908.9 ('...could be catastrophic'), so start no earlier than 909.0 and confirm the speaker boundary by ear. A longer version runs to 919.1 ('...fearing for his own life almost in the bell, it was going to be ripped off the wall and take him down with it').

clips.speaker: Chris Lemons
clips.words_en: that realisation that hope is lost, because that's certainly how it felt. That I'm powerless, powerless, certainly powerless to do anything to help myself or save myself.
clips.notes: Acceptance. Clean, with a noise floor around -47 dB.

clips.speaker: Chris Lemons
clips.words_en: But yeah, it's a very sad, depressing moment really to find yourself in this completely alien place
clips.notes: Very clean (floor about -50 dB). It can run on to 1210.95: '...lonely essentially, you know, it's dark and lonely down there' (8.9 s total).

clips.speaker: Chris Lemons
clips.words_en: mostly you think of the damage you're going to do to the people you're leaving behind, the carnage that's going to be... left
clips.notes: Clean.

clips.speaker: Chris Lemons
clips.words_en: I can remember actually calling out apologising to her several times, you know, screaming up into the air, I'm saying, I'm very, I'm so sorry Morag, I'm so sorry
clips.notes: Very powerful. 'her' and 'Morag' are his then-fiancee, now wife. It is personal, so handle respectfully. BBC music (tones at 469/625/820 Hz) starts at about 1263.0, so end by 1262.85.

Five files are downloaded to /home/user/aireels/assets/lemons_media/, which is gitignored and not in git status. Durations from ffprobe:
- BBC Outlook p08lg6lt: 2125.0 s
- BBC 5 Live Eye of the Storm p07c6w6z: 1327.1 s

- Roll With The Punches EP242: 3788.7 s
- The You Project #679: 3093.6 s

All clip times are seconds in those local files. Transcripts are in /home/user/aireels/assets/lemons_media/transcripts/. The medium_*.json files hold word-level timestamps (faster-whisper medium, int8, en, beam 5) for every recommended range. The locator_small_* files are full-episode whisper-small transcripts used only to find the ranges.

OFFSET WARNING: a sibling agent's Outlook locator uses the other BBC version, vpid p0776q29 (2141 s). Cross-correlation gives p0776q29 time = p08lg6lt time + 15.6 s, and the offset is constant. All Outlook times above are for p08lg6lt.

BEST SOURCE
- BBC Outlook (2019) has full-band studio audio (rolloff about 7-8 kHz) and covers every moment wanted: snag, bailout, snap and darkness, acceptance, 'I'm so sorry Morag', calling for Duncan, gas running out, 'this was it', waking and seeing Duncan, feeling fine, reunion, return to the sea.
- BBC Eye of the Storm is clean with no music, but Lemons is on a narrower-band line.
- The Big Interview is a telephone-band line with a music bed under his clips. Fallback only.
- Roll With The Punches and The You Project are wide-band (about 6-7 kHz) long-form backups, downloaded but NOT transcribed.

MUSIC AND ARCHIVAL CHECKS
I checked each clip's noise floor and the tonality of its quiet frames. Clips marked clean have noise-like floors at about -45 to -60 dB.

AVOID these ranges:
- Eye of the Storm 42-87 s: a clip from the Last Breath documentary played by the host ('Here's a clip... I was completely alone... five or six minutes in this bailout').
- Outlook (the presenter thanks Dogwoof 'for letting us use those recordings'):
  - about 435-446: swell SFX
  - about 620-632: 'this is a recording from the day'
  - about 858-866: archival comms 'slack diver 2'
  - 1020.75-1043: BBC bang SFX plus music
  - 1071-1080: music
  - 1263-1271: music
  - 1594.1-1595.4: archival 'OK Dave, you're clear to go'
- Outlook 1546-1563: a music bed under the dive supervisor's ROV description.
- Outlook 0-13 s: a trailer for another BBC programme.

DAVE YUASA AND DUNCAN ALLCOCK
I found NO downloadable audio of either man speaking. Searches covered BBC, CBC, NPR, podcasts and STV/P&J. Coverage says Yuasa keeps a low profile and still dives, and Allcock retired in 2024. Their voices appear to exist only in Last Breath (2019) and film-promo video, which are excluded.

Substitutes:
- Lemons describing Dave and Duncan.
- The Bibby Topaz dive supervisor, Craig Frederick, in his own voice in BBC Outlook. The name is as the presenter says it; verify spelling. At Outlook 1673.65 he recalls Duncan reporting 'he's alive, he's breathing, he's actually talking'. These are not Duncan's own words.

SOURCES NOT DOWNLOADED
- CBC The Current, 2025-03-17, 'Stranded, this diver lost oxygen for 25 minutes. He survived' (about 19:46, Matt Galloway; page cbc.ca/radio/thecurrent/lemons-diving-survival-story-1.7487922). It is no longer in the podcast RSS. My one direct fetch of the asset URL listed in the page's player data was blocked by the session's permission system as bot-check circumvention, so I stopped. The user could fetch it manually if wanted.
- Taproom Talks (Buzzsprout, Nov 2025): the CloudFront edge returned 403, not circumvented.
- Newstalk Moncrieff 'Last Breath' (Apr 2019): the player is JS-only, no direct enclosure found.
- NPR/WAMC 2025 'Last Breath' item: a Simu Liu interview, not Lemons.
- Not checked: Pretty Sure I Can Fly (Knoxville, Dec 2024), BiG Scuba ep163, Exceed High Performance (Sep 2025), GB News and ITV video.
- YouTube was not attempted.

NUMBER DISPUTES (flag on screen)
- Bailout gas:
  - Lemons: '5 to 6 minutes' (Outlook), '5, 6, 7 minutes' (Eye of the Storm), '6 or 7' and 'maybe 7, 8 minutes' (Big Interview).
  - Supervisor Craig Frederick: 'five minutes is a little bit lean... more between nine and ten minutes' (Outlook 1416.3).
- Time without gas or until rescue:
  - Lemons: best guess 'about 25 minutes' without oxygen (Eye of the Storm, about 986 s); '30, 35 minutes with nothing to breathe' (Outlook 1773); 'about 35 minutes between the umbilical severing and being back in position', with about 20 minutes assumed without gas (Eye of the Storm, about 720 s); 'nearly 40 minutes' to fix the boat and 'those 40 minutes' (Big Interview).
  - Supervisor: regained control in 'maybe 20 minutes'; Dave was able to dive at '35 minutes probably' (Outlook).
  - Presenters say 'around 35' and 'more than 25'.
- Depth: Lemons says '90 meters' (Big Interview) and that the ship was '90 metres above us' (Eye of the Storm). Presenters say 100 m.
- Drift distance: about 200 m (Eye of the Storm), 240 m (Big Interview), 'maybe 250 metres' (supervisor, Outlook).
- Fall to the seabed: about 10 m (Eye of the Storm, Big Interview) or 10-11 m (Outlook).
- Weather: 30-35 knots with a 5-6 m swell (Outlook); about 30 knots and 4-5 m (Eye of the Storm); 35-40 knots and 4-5 m (Big Interview).
- Time of day: Big Interview says about 10 pm.
- Duration of bailout before the snap: Lemons says the umbilical snapped 'maybe 10 seconds after I turned that on' (Eye of the Storm 446.6).

ATTRIBUTION FOR ON-SCREEN CREDITS
- 'BBC World Service, Outlook (2019)'
- 'BBC Radio 5 Live, Eye of the Storm (2019)'
- 'The Big Interview podcast (2021)'

RESPECT NOTES
The 'I'm so sorry Morag' line names his wife. It is his own public account, but use it with care. Several lines are Lemons paraphrasing Dave ('in his words... rescue a dead body'); credit them as Lemons' words.

ASR CAVEATS
Verify by ear: 'fetus-like' (probably 'foetal'), 'window' (probably 'wind down'), 'death' (should be 'debt'), and the 'Frederick' spelling. Start and end times are padded about 0.05-0.2 s from the word timestamps; leave 0.1-0.2 s fades.

draft.caption_ko:
[실화] 수심 약 90m, 생명줄이 끊긴 잠수사
※ 실제 인터뷰 음성(BBC)이 포함되어 있습니다.

2012년 9월 18일 밤, 스코틀랜드 애버딘에서 동쪽으로 약 200km 떨어진 북해 헌팅턴 유전에서 일어난 일입니다. 잠수지원선 비비 토파즈(Bibby Topaz)에서 내려간 포화잠수사 크리스 레몬스(당시 32세)와 데이브 유아사는 수심 약 90m의 해저 구조물에서 일하고 있었고, 다이빙 벨 안에는 벨맨 던컨 올콕이 있었습니다.

밤 10시 10분쯤 배의 동적위치제어(DP) 장치가 고장 나 배가 바람(약 30노트)에 밀려났습니다. 그 사이 레몬스의 생명줄(엄빌리컬)이 구조물에 걸려 끊어졌습니다. 그는 완전한 어둠 속에서 등에 멘 비상 기체(헬륨·산소 혼합 기체)로 버티며 구조물 위로 올라갔지만, 결국 의식을 잃었습니다. 선장과 일등항해사가 배를 수동으로 몰아 되돌렸고, DP를 다시 켜서 배가 제자리로 돌아오자 유아사가 그를 벨까지 끌고 왔습니다. 올콕이 헬멧을 벗기고 구조 호흡을 두 번 하자 그는 숨을 들이켜며 깨어났습니다. 감압을 마친 뒤 검사에서 뇌 손상은 발견되지 않았고, 약 3주 뒤 같은 세 사람이 같은 현장으로 돌아가 작업을 마쳤습니다.

📌 출처마다 다른 숫자
· 수심: 80m / 90m / 91m / 100m
· 비상 기체: 레몬스 본인도 2019년에는 5~6분, 2025년에는 8~9분이라고 말했고, 잠수 감독관은 9~10분이라고 했습니다. 2022년 의학 사례 보고(Dreyer 외, Healthcare)는 실린더 용량으로 계산하면 5분보다 훨씬 길었을 수 있다고 봅니다(계산 모델이며 측정값은 아님).
· 생명줄이 끊긴 뒤 구조까지: 약 33~41분입니다. 실제로 숨 쉴 기체 없이 버틴 시간이나 의식을 잃은 시각은 아무도 모릅니다. "산소 없이 40분"이라는 표현은 이 두 숫자를 섞은 것입니다.
· 구조 직후 상태: 올콕과 레몬스의 증언에는 구조 호흡 두 번 뒤 깨어났다고 나오지만, 회사와 IMCA 보고서에는 "의식 없음, 호흡 있음"으로 적혀 있습니다.
· 배가 밀려난 거리: 190~250m

어떻게 살아남았는지는 아직 확실하지 않습니다. 차가운 수온이 뇌의 산소 소모를 줄였다는 가설 등이 거론되지만 모두 가설입니다. 사고 원인은 DP 제어 통신망 장애와 하드웨어 결함으로 조사됐고, 운용자의 잘못은 지적되지 않았습니다(IMCA 안전 공지 02/13, 영국 HSE 안전 공지 OSD 1-2013).

음성 출처: BBC World Service 「Outlook」(2019, 진행 Emily Webb). 크리스 레몬스와 당시 잠수 감독관 크레이그 프레드릭의 인터뷰입니다. 다큐멘터리 「Last Breath」(2019)와 영화 「Last Breath」(2025)의 영상·음악·실제 교신 음성은 쓰지 않았습니다. 모든 그림은 직접 그린 일러스트이며, 실제 인물의 얼굴은 그리지 않았습니다. 이 사고에서는 모두 살아남았습니다.

#북해 #포화잠수 #잠수사 #실화 #생존 #사건사고 #ChrisLemons #LastBreath

checks.verdict:
The script is mostly accurate and carefully hedged. Before publishing, fix one factual error and four misleading compressions. Everything else is minor wording or visual cleanup.

**Confirmed against sources:**
- 18 Sep 2012 was a Tuesday (checked with `date`).
- Age 32: 2012 press, the 2022 case report and CBC all say 32.
- About 200 km east of Aberdeen: BBC Future gives 204 km; the case report gives 200 km.
- Depth range 80/90/91/100 m.
- About 22:10 alarms and 30 knots of wind (Bibby statement, posted on gCaptain 25 Sep 2012).
- Drift of 240 m (Bibby 2012 and IMCA), 190 m (Bibby 2015, offshore-energy) and 250 m (Frederick, Outlook).
- Bridge timeline: manual control by the Master and Chief Officer at 22:17, back over the site at 22:40, on the bell stage at 22:46, inside the bell at 22:48.
- Time from the snap to rescue: 33 minutes (case report) to 41 minutes (Lemons' NIBA 2025 slides do show '35 Minutes' and '41 Minutes').
- Bailout duration: 8–9 minutes (CBC 2025) and 9–10 minutes (Frederick on Outlook).
- About 3 weeks later, the same three people returned to the same place and finished the job (BBC News, BBC Future, OGV, Outlook).
- About 4 days of decompression.
- The BBC Future closing quote is verbatim.
- HSE OSD 1-2013 is dated 23 Jan 2013.
- The Outlook presenter is Emily Webb.

**Audio clips:** I re-transcribed all five clips with faster-whisper medium, with and without 3 s of surrounding audio. The words match `words_en`. The 'alive' clip is Craig Frederick: the episode's outro names 'Chris Lemons and Craig Frederick', and the surrounding talk is clearly the supervisor relaying what Duncan told him. The dark clip says 'you plunge' in both passes.

**One factual error:** IMCA Safety Flash 02/13 does not say 'unconscious but breathing'. Only Bibby's 2012 statement says that. The script repeats this mistake in the breaths visual and in the caption.

**Misleading compressions:**
- The 2019 bailout figure is given as 5–6 minutes, but BBC Future 2019 quotes him saying 6–7.
- The curl segment says curling up 'saved gas'.
- The 'back' visual shows three divers in the water.
- The caption says the cause was found to be hardware faults, but IMCA says no definitive cause was found.

**Sourcing and rights risks:**
- The IMCA and HSE notices are anonymised; they never name the Bibby Topaz.
- The Outlook episode includes 'Last Breath' recordings supplied by Dogwoof (the outro thanks them). The music under the end of the dark clip needs checking before the caption says no 'Last Breath' audio was used.
- The audio file and the source URL in the script are a 22 Jul 2020 re-release in the Outlook Podcast Archive. The original episode is p0776q29, 23 Apr 2019.

issues.problem: The script says both the company and IMCA recorded him as 'unconscious but breathing'. IMCA Safety Flash 02/13 says no such thing. It says Diver 2, 'now unconscious, was recovered by Diver 1' and 'recovered consciousness shortly after his recovery back to the bell'; breathing is never mentioned. Only Bibby's own 2012 statement (reposted on gCaptain) says 'unconscious but breathing ... regained consciousness when his helmet was removed'. Note also that the 2012 press, which was based on Bibby's information, reported 'After two breaths by the bellman he started breathing on his own'.

In the clip used in this reel he says 'Five minutes'. His 2019 range is therefore 5–7 minutes, not 5–6. issues.problem: The narration '몸을 웅크려 기체를 아꼈지만' presents curling up as how he saved gas. Lemons says two separate things. To conserve gas, he calmed down: 'I took a measured decision to calm down and conserve what little gas I had left.' He curled up because he expected no rescue: 'I didn't expect to be rescued, so I just curled up into a ball' (BBC Future). CBC adds that he lay in the fetal position where he had the best odds of being found. That breathing became harder is supported ('It takes more effort to suck the gas down' in BBC Future; 'a little bit tighter, a little bit harder to suck it down' on Outlook).

checks.verdict:
I re-transcribed all five clips from the local BBC Outlook file (p08lg6lt) with faster-whisper medium and word timestamps. I also cross-checked them with the small model, forced scoring of alternative transcripts, start/end probes, and RMS/spectral analysis. Speakers and wording hold up, but four of the five cut points need moving, and two clips have hidden BBC music.

**Speakers and quotes**
- Four clips are Chris Lemons. The context is first person and his pitch is about 110–120 Hz. clip_alive is Craig Frederick (about 150 Hz; the context and The Independent confirm the name and spelling).
- No presenter (Emily Webb) speech is inside any range.
- The BBC Future closing quote is verbatim: Richard Gray, 23 Apr 2019, 'One of the greatest reasons I survived was the quality of the people around me'.
- The 'shotgun' tag is confirmed: Eye of the Storm 'snapped with a really violent sort of shotgun sound', and Outlook 'outrageous shotgun bang'.
- The file is the Outlook Podcast Archive re-release (22 Jul 2020) of the episode first published 23 Apr 2019. Crediting it as '(2019)' is fine.

**Problems found**
- clip_8000t: the start at 817.45 drops 'the' and clips 'sort', so the clip is heard as 'So the weight…'.
- clip_math: it is not clean. A BBC tone (about 1.5 kHz plus 248/496 Hz) fades in under 'this is… this is not going to end well at all' from about 1161.0 s, and its start clips the /f/ of 'Five'.
- clip_dark: the music drone is exposed after 1070.80, and a 1 kHz music line is already faintly present from about 1069.6.
- clip_alive: the start chops 'He' (its onset is at 1673.48, not 1673.68).
- clip_thisisit: a quiet music chord starts right after 'hurt'.
- clip_dark: 'you plunge' vs 'a plunge' stays unresolved. The Korean subtitle works either way.

**Corrected ranges**

|---|---|---|

| clip_dark | 1065.66–1070.80 | high-pass 90 Hz, notch 1000 Hz and 248 Hz, fade-out 0.06 s |

**Other fixes**
- The breaths tag credits the 'two breaths' to Allcock himself, but that count comes from Frederick and Lemons.
- The caption says Lemons gave 5–6 minutes of bailout in 2019. His 2019 statements actually range from 5 to 7 minutes.
- The 'curl' narration slightly conflates his reasons: he saved gas by calming down, and curled up because he didn't expect rescue. Low severity.

Not verified: the exact word in 'Suddenly [you/a] plunge', which needs a listen by ear.

The script is accurate, well hedged and respectful, and it's close to ready, but it needs one tightening pass before TTS.

1. **Runtime.** It will run about 107–110 s, not about 100. The narration has about 420 syllables. Okene's final timeline puts the Hyunsu +18% + clone voice at 5.78 syllables/s, with about 0.69 s of padding per narration scene and 0.55 s per clip. That gives about 84 s of narration plus 26.7 s of clips. The script's own est_seconds already add up to 104.7 s, and Okene finished at 112.9 s.
2. **Hook.** The hook never says whose lifeline it is. The first real voice doesn't arrive until about 25 s, but Okene put one at 4.4 s.
3. **Unclear by ear.** Several lines are hard to follow when heard once:
   - '벨로 돌아가던 그의 생명줄' (it sounds like the lifeline was going back to the bell)
   - '비상 기체를 연 직후' ('연' is one bare syllable)
   - '몇 분 분량' (stutters in TTS)
   - '배를 손으로 몰아' (sounds literal, as if steering with his hands)
   - '같은 자리' (could mean a seat)
4. **Wording against the sources.**
   - In BBC Outlook, Lemons describes creaking, then the comms line crackling, then the parting, so '직후' overstates how fast it happened.
   - '숨이 뻑뻑해졌다' is an awkward rendering of 'tighter, a little bit harder to suck it down'.
   - The gasp after two rescue breaths is stated as plain fact, but company and IMCA reports record 'unconscious, breathing'.

The gauge line is sourced ('too dark for me to see it', BBC Outlook audio at about 22:18), so keep that image. Give every number a `tts` value, glued so the word counts match: 구십미터, 이천십이년 구월, 열시쯤, 삼십오분, 삼주.

final.caption_ko:
[실화] 수심 약 90m, 생명줄이 끊긴 잠수사
※ 실제 인터뷰 음성(BBC)이 포함되어 있습니다.

2012년 9월 18일 밤, 스코틀랜드 애버딘에서 동쪽으로 약 200km 떨어진 북해 헌팅턴 유전에서 일어난 일입니다. 잠수지원선 비비 토파즈(Bibby Topaz)에서 내려간 포화잠수사 크리스 레몬스(당시 32세)와 데이브 유아사가 수심 약 90m의 해저 구조물에서 일하고 있었고, 다이빙 벨 안에는 벨맨 던컨 올콕이 있었습니다.

밤 10시 10분쯤, 배를 제자리에 붙잡아 두던 동적위치제어(DP) 시스템이 고장 나 배가 바람(약 30~35노트)에 밀려났습니다. 그 사이 레몬스의 생명줄(엄빌리컬)이 구조물에 걸려 끊어졌습니다. 그는 완전한 어둠 속에서 등에 멘 비상 기체(헬륨·산소 혼합 기체)로 버티며 구조물 위로 올라갔지만, 결국 의식을 잃었습니다. 선장과 일등항해사가 배를 수동으로 몰아 되돌렸고, DP를 다시 켜서 배가 제자리로 돌아오자 유아사가 그를 벨까지 끌고 왔습니다. 생명줄이 끊긴 지 약 35분 뒤, 올콕이 헬멧을 벗기고 구조 호흡을 두 번 하자 그가 숨을 들이켜며 깨어났다고 BBC와 동료들은 전합니다(구조 직후 상태는 기록마다 조금 다릅니다. 아래 참고). 약 4일간 감압을 마친 뒤 받은 검사에서 이상은 발견되지 않았고, 약 3주 뒤 같은 세 사람(잠수사 2명·벨맨 1명)이 같은 현장으로 돌아가 작업을 마쳤습니다.

📌 출처마다 다른 숫자와 기록
· 수심: 80m / 90m / 91m / 100m
· 비상 기체: 레몬스 본인도 2019년에는 5~7분(BBC 뉴스·Outlook 5~6분, BBC Future 6~7분), 2025년 CBC 인터뷰에서는 8~9분이라고 했고, 잠수 감독관 크레이그 프레드릭은 9~10분(2019 Outlook)이라고 했습니다. 2022년 의학 사례 보고(Dreyer 외, Healthcare)는 실린더 용량으로 계산하면 5분보다 훨씬 길었을 수 있다고 봅니다(계산 모델이며 측정값은 아님).
· 생명줄이 끊긴 뒤 구조까지: 약 33~41분입니다. 실제로 숨 쉴 기체 없이 버틴 시간이나 의식을 잃은 시각은 아무도 모릅니다. "산소 없이 40분"이라는 표현은 이 두 숫자를 섞은 것입니다.
· 구조 직후 상태: BBC 보도와 잠수 감독관의 증언에는 올콕이 구조 호흡을 두 번 하자 숨을 들이켰다고 나오고, 올콕 본인도 그가 숨을 확 들이켰다고 회상합니다(Independent, 2019). 반면 2012년 회사(비비) 발표에는 "의식은 없지만 호흡 있음, 헬멧을 벗기자 의식 회복"으로, IMCA 공지에는 "의식 없음 → 벨로 옮긴 직후 의식 회복"으로만 적혀 있습니다.
· 비상 기체를 연 순서: 레몬스 본인은 호스가 막혀 비상 기체를 연 뒤 생명줄이 끊어졌다고 말하지만, 회사·IMCA 기록에는 끊어진 직후 비상 기체로 전환했다고 적혀 있습니다.
· 배가 밀려난 거리: 190~250m

어떻게 살아남았는지는 아직 확실하지 않습니다. 차가운 수온이 뇌의 산소 소모를 줄였다는 가설 등이 거론되지만 모두 가설입니다.

사고는 DP 제어 시스템의 내부 통신망(RBUS)이 막히면서 일어난 것으로 조사됐습니다. 근본 원인은 확정되지 않았고, 점검에서 하드웨어 결함 여러 건이 발견됐습니다. 공지는 운용자 과실을 언급하지 않았고, IMCA 공지에는 구조에 참여한 선내 인원들이 전문성과 팀워크, 침착함을 인정받았다고 적혀 있습니다(IMCA 안전 공지 02/13, 영국 HSE 안전 공지 OSD 1-2013 · 두 문서 모두 선박명은 익명 처리됐지만 세부 내용이 이 사고와 일치).

음성 출처: BBC World Service 「Outlook」 "How did this diver cheat death?"(2019년 4월 23일 방송, 2020년 아카이브 재공개본에서 발췌, 진행 Emily Webb). 크리스 레몬스와 당시 잠수 감독관 크레이그 프레드릭의 인터뷰 발언만 짧게 발췌했습니다. 다큐멘터리 「Last Breath」(2019)와 영화 「Last Breath」(2025)의 영상·음악·실제 교신 음성은 쓰지 않았습니다. 모든 그림은 직접 그린 일러스트이며, 실제 인물의 얼굴은 그리지 않았습니다. 이 사고에서는 모두 살아남았습니다.
